A target at half maximum HP or more takes S d8 necrotic on failure, half on success. A target below half maximum HP instead takes 2 S d8 necrotic on failure, half on success. Determine the threshold before rolling damage.

source.originalText: Flesh to Ash: Create an AoE burst that doubles damage if target is below 50% HP.

cards.name: Corpse Gateway
cards.rangeAndTarget: One visible corpse within 60 feet and one unoccupied space within 5 feet of it
cards.effect: Corpse Gateway. Tags: mage-spell, lich, teleportation, corpse. Teleport to the chosen unoccupied space adjacent to a visible corpse. The corpse is not consumed or altered. Summoned-companion remains, repeated fragments of the same destroyed creature and illusory corpses are not legal anchors. This non-elemental spell clears an active Nuke Chain.

source.originalText: Corpse Gateway: Teleport to a corpse within line of sight.

cards.name: Soulbound Ritual
cards.rangeAndTarget: One of your destroyed bound elite undead companions within 30 feet or its inert binding token
cards.effect: Soulbound Ritual. Tags: mage-spell, lich, companion, resurrection. Return one destroyed Boneflayer, Dreadblade or Wraithbound to an unoccupied space within 30 feet at half its maximum HP. It gains S+M temporary HP for 1 minute. The returned companion remains subject to the shared Companion Command limit and cannot create a corpse, XP, loot or resource event if destroyed again.

source.originalText: Soulbound Ritual: Revive a fallen undead pet with bonus stats.

cards.name: Resonance Apex — NEW Playtest Capstone
cards.rangeAndTarget: One Mage spell you are beginning to cast
cards.effect: Before paying for one Mage spell, reduce that spell's printed RP cost by up to 10 RP, minimum final cost 0. This capstone is new playtest design and is not claimed as a recovered historical feature. The cast cannot also use Resonance Surge or generic Overcast. It remains one spell cast, follows ordinary Focus/Nuke Chain rules, and alters Dissonance only through rules that would already apply to that cast.

completeCurrentEnvelope.authoringNotes: Provisional; editorial review applied; human table balance testing required

completeCurrentEnvelope.protectedInterfaceOriginal: The first replay of a newly Mirrorbound Echo ignores Refrain Dissonance; repeating the same stored Echo builds Refrain normally.
engine: Intelligence is the class ability; use d8 Hit Die from the detailed book, recording the older runtime d6 as superseded for this draft. You begin with 3 empty Echo Slots. Expansion II raises ordinary capacity 5; Sacred/Floating memory features may add one restricted slot, but total concurrent stored Echoes never exceeds 6. Slots are storage, not spell slots. Releasing normally empties that record. Rest restores RP, not spent Echoes. Starting a new encounter does not duplicate the archive.

Mirrorbind is an Action, once per encounter, against a creature within 60 ft whose eligible ability you saw resolve since the start of your previous turn. Target must have INT 6 or lower, not be a boss or possess unique/legendary status unless an encounter script explicitly permits copying. It makes WIS save versus class DC; failure captures one witnessed ability into an empty slot. No copying from allies, your companions, another copy, a corpse, a recharge-limited legendary power or an at-will source that itself restores resources. You can voluntarily erase a slot without an action on your turn, permanently losing its record.

Record source creature/name, witnessed ability, category, damage type, allowed rank, capture encounter and whether first release has occurred. For this pilot, capture copies the observed role into ONE bounded profile: Strike=one target 60 ft class spell attack S d8 observed damage type; Burst=up to 3 enemies in 10 ft radius within 30 ft DEX save S d6, half on success; Mend=one living ally 30 ft S d6+M HP; Ward=one ally 30 ft S d6+M temporary HP for 1 minute; Hindrance=one enemy 30 ft WIS save or Speed-10 ft and no Reactions until end its next turn. Choose only a profile actually expressed by the observed source; physical attack cannot become healing. Rank is max(1, ceil(source challenge rating/2)); if source lacks a rating the Director assigns a rank before the encounter, not after seeing a desirable ability. Rank cannot exceed your Mirrorsage learnable rank; no copying character levels from a creature. Damage/targets/control are capped by these profiles, not source boss dice.

Echo Release costs the Core V 2 RP cost of the recorded rank, minimum 2, consumes its record and counts as a spell for Dissonance and Refrain. Spell attack/DC use your own stats. First release of a newly captured record ignores Refrain addition only; base strain remains. Any preserved subsequent release uses ordinary repeated-spell strain. All released Echoes, pet replays, fusions and reflections share ONE release action per round; a specifically combined package counts once but pays for every component and has its printed damage cap. Copies cannot create resources or recursive Echoes.

One Mirror Beast OR Reflective Companion, never both. Mirror Beast uses standard companion stats, initially copies appearance only, and costs a Bonus Action to command. You may command it to make its normal attack OR originate your round's Echo Release from its position, paying RP and consuming the record normally; not both. You still supply an Action for release unless a feature specifically changes that action cost. A shifted appearance grants no extra actions/stats. Destroying/dismissing it grants no capture, corpse, XP or recovery. Charm Bind is 1/long rest, 3 rounds, concentration, INT 6-or-lower target WIS save and repeat at each turn end/when harmed by your side; never a player character or boss without explicit encounter permission. A charmed companion uses its own ordinary attack with damage capped at standard companion S d6; unique spells/powers remain unavailable.

Focus Point is a separate resource: when Mimicry Focus is known, receive 1 at encounter start, maximum 1, lost at encounter end. It can modify one Echo without generating another release, recapture or resource refund. No stacking damage doublings; use the printed modest die/range boost. Healing/support copies always consume RP and cannot restore RP or duplicate limited-use features.

Standard acquisition applies; baseline Mirrorbind, Echo Release and summon procedure become usable by selecting their cards. Echo Channeling and Mirrorcall are upgrades, not duplicate mandatory unlocks. The contradiction between source initial 3 slots and Expansion I 2→3 is reconciled as an archive-safety upgrade below. Perfect Reflection automatic 9, Hero choice 10, corresponding Final 20. The finale does not override copy eligibility or the shared release cap.
workedExample: Mirrorsage 5, INT 16, PB 3, S 2, M 3, RP 9, three slots; know Mirrorbind, Echo Release, Mirror Beast Summon, Reflective Shield at 1, Beast Instinct and Reflective Pulse at 2; Mimicry Focus and Reflective Analysis at 3. Begin with Focus 1.
Turn 1: witness an eligible serpent's rank 1 poison cone, then Mirrorbind on your turn. It fails WIS save; store Burst/poison/rank 1. RP stays 9; one encounter capture spent.

Turn 2: Echo Release is Action and 2 RP, RP 9→7; empty the stored slot. Up to 3 enemies roll DEX against 14 for 2d6 poison, half on success. First release ignores Refrain but still adds 1 base Dissonance.
Turn 3: without another stored Echo you cannot simply release again. Use a weapon or ordinary legal spell. A short rest restores RP but not the consumed record.

Alternative turn 2: summon Mirror Beast for 2 RP, leaving RP 7 and the Echo stored. On turn 3 use Action Echo Release plus Bonus Action command to originate it from the Beast, pay 2 RP, ending 5; the Beast cannot also attack that round.
A failed Mirrorbind capture still expends its encounter attempt. Beast Instinct's limited retry may help if known; a boss excluded by eligibility cannot be made eligible with a high roll.
balanceQuestions: Is the initial capture dependency enjoyable with an empty archive?
Are bounded profiles diverse enough without importing boss actions?
Does the shared release/companion budget keep fusions and clones manageable?

cards.name: Echo Channeling
cards.rangeAndTarget: Your own Echo Release
cards.effect: After releasing an Echo, add M to one target's damage or healing. No modifier to resource effects; this upgrade does not grant another release or repeat the source's rider.

source.originalText: Echo Channeling: Cast a stored Echo ability. Consumes a slot.

cards.name: Mirrorcall
cards.rangeAndTarget: Your Mirror Beast
cards.effect: Beast gains+M maximum/current HP when summoned and+5 ft Speed. Echo Release or Mirror Beast Summon already provides its base procedure; this is an optional enhancement, not a second required unlock.

source.originalText: Mirrorcall: Summon a Mirror Beast that mimics one stored Echo ability.

cards.name: Echo Slot Expansion I
cards.rangeAndTarget: One newly bound record
cards.effect: If an ordinary slot is full, replace one record while preserving its name/profile in an inert backup. Once before next long rest, after a slot empties, restore that backup without an Action. Total usable records remain at your capacity; backup cannot be cast directly or backed up again. An inert backup counts toward the absolute six-record archive ceiling. A backup cannot be created if usable records plus inert backups would exceed six.

source.originalText: Echo Slot Expansion I: Increase slots from 2 → 3.

cards.name: Reflective Pulse
cards.rangeAndTarget: Attacker within 30 ft after its first hit this round damages you
cards.effect: Deal psychic damage equal to min(M, damage actually taken). This cannot critically hit, trigger another reflection, generate resources or prevent the original damage. No effect if you take 0.

source.originalText: Reflective Pulse: First hit you take each round returns 10% damage.

cards.name: Beast Instinct
cards.rangeAndTarget: A failed Mirrorbind against eligible INT 6-or-lower source
cards.effect: Force that target to reroll its successful save; use the second result. Eligibility, line of effect and an empty slot still required. Does not create a second captured record or a new encounter attempt.

source.originalText: Beast Instinct: +10% chance to capture Echoes from INT ≤ 6 creatures.

cards.name: Mirrorbind
cards.rangeAndTarget: One eligible witnessed creature within 60 ft
cards.effect: Apply the engine's exact capture procedure: WIS save or store a bounded profile for the witnessed ability. State category/rank before save. Success prevents capture but consumes attempt; no target can be mirrored outside eligibility restrictions.

source.originalText: Mirrorbind: Attempt to capture an ability you've just witnessed, storing it in an Echo Slot if successful.

cards.name: Echo Release
cards.cost: Recorded rank RP cost; consume 1 Echo
cards.rangeAndTarget: Profile target/range
cards.effect: Resolve the stored Strike/Burst/Mend/Ward/Hindrance profile, using current S and INT. Pay before release; empty slot even if resisted. First release ignores only Refrain addition. No original source extra actions/resources/procs.

source.originalText: Echo Release: Cast a stored Echo ability, consuming the slot.

cards.name: Mirror Beast Summon
cards.rangeAndTarget: One empty space within 15 ft
cards.effect: Summon one standard Mirror Beast; replaces any prior Beast/Reflective Companion. Choose appearance of a stored source. It attacks only on Bonus Action command or originates your paid release with Action+command, never both. No copied anatomy, regeneration or immortality.

source.originalText: Mirror Beast Summon: Call forth a Mirror Beast that can use one of your stored Echo abilities.

cards.name: Charm Creature
cards.rangeAndTarget: One eligible INT 6-or-lower creature within 30 ft
cards.effect: WIS save or become Reflective Companion under engine restrictions. It repeats save at turn end and when harmed by your side. Replaces Mirror Beast; on end original disposition returns. Requires no suicidal orders; cannot force beliefs or permanently enslave.

source.originalText: Charm Creature: Attempt to temporarily charm a low-intelligence creature to fight alongside you.

cards.name: Reflective Shield
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self when hit by an attack from within 60 ft
cards.effect: Gain+2 AC against triggering attack, potentially making it miss. If it misses, attacker takes M force damage. This is bounded retaliation, not copying the original attack; cannot trigger another reflection or capture.

source.originalText: Reflective Shield: Create a brief defensive barrier that has a chance to reflect the next attack back at the attacker.

cards.name: Advanced Mirrorcall
cards.rangeAndTarget: Your Mirror Beast
cards.effect: You may change Beast appearance to another stored source as a Bonus Action without resummoning or restoring HP. It gains either+10 ft swim or climb Speed until it ends. No new release, attack or capture.

source.originalText: Advanced Mirrorcall: Mirror Beast can now shift once per fight into a new form based on a second Echo.

cards.name: Echo Slot Expansion II
cards.rangeAndTarget: Your archive
cards.effect: Ordinary Echo storage capacity becomes 5, replacing 3. Restricted extra slots still obey total 6. New slots are empty; the feature creates no Echo records or spell access.

source.originalText: Echo Slot Expansion II: Max Echo Slots: 5

cards.name: Dual Echo Cast
cards.cost: RP for each of 2 Echoes; consume both
cards.rangeAndTarget: One target per eligible profile
cards.effect: Release two records captured from different creatures as ONE combined release. Each deals/heals half its profile's rolled amount, round once per component. At most one Hindrance rider; no duplicated resources or additional release this round.

source.originalText: Dual Echo Cast: Spend 2 Echoes in one turn; must be from different creatures.

cards.name: Mimicry Focus
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self
cards.effect: At genuine encounter start gain 1 Focus Point, cap 1; any previous point is replaced. Spend on Focus Channel or pay 1 Focus during a release to add 1d6 to one damage/healing target. No point generation from staged combat.

cards.name: Mirror Shell
cards.rangeAndTarget: A hostile spell targeting only you within 60 ft
cards.effect: After a successful save against the spell or after its spell attack misses, choose its caster; it makes WIS save or takes S d8 force. Original damage/control follow normal results. No copying arbitrary spell text or redirecting an area spell.

cards.name: Perfect Reflection
cards.rangeAndTarget: Creature within 60 ft whose observed ability targets you
cards.effect: Reduce triggering damage to you by(S+1)d8+M, minimum 0. If any is prevented, source makes WIS save or takes that prevented amount as force, maximum 30. This is your release action for the round; no reflected conditions or legendary powers. Cannot recursively reflect.

cards.name: Echo Fusion
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to 2 profile targets within 30 ft
cards.effect: Choose two stored profiles. Resolve one at full dice and the other at half dice to one target each. Only one may be healing; at most one Hindrance rider. Counts as one combined release and cannot receive Dual Echo Cast simultaneously.

cards.name: Mirror Shift
cards.rangeAndTarget: Your Mirror Beast within 60 ft
cards.effect: Switch its appearance to a stored source and choose swim 30 ft or climb 30 ft until next shift. Restore no HP or attacks; no flight, incorporeality or copied creature special actions. Does not release or consume the Echo.

source.originalText: Mirror Shift: Command your Mirror Beast to change form, adopting a different stored Echo ability.

cards.name: Focus Channel
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self; next release this turn

cards.name: Mirror Image

cards.name: Fractured Dominion

cards.name: Corrupt Echo

cards.effect: Add 1d6 necrotic to one target on release OR force one damaged target to make WIS save or lose Reactions until end its next turn. No double rider or additional release. Added die is excluded from later copies.

cards.effect: On start and each later Bonus Action+1 RP pulse, WIS save: S d6 psychic, half on success. Failure also loses Reactions until start your next turn. At most 3 pulses. Zone is not an Echo source or resource generator.

completeCurrentEnvelope.authoringNotes: Provisional; notebook adversarial findings reconciled and source-preserving editorial review complete. Human balance testing remains.

completeCurrentEnvelope.protectedInterfaceOriginal: Smite, Aura, and Lay on Hands are Oath mechanics and do not generate Weave Dissonance. After a successful melee hit, the next Oath spell before the end of the next turn generates 1 less Dissonance.
engine: Charisma governs Oath DC/M and divine technique attacks. Weapon attacks use their ordinary Strength/Dexterity ability. Hit Die d10; all armor, shields, simple and martial weapons. Paladin has no Conviction or Oracle Revelation Charges. Lay on Hands is its own pool, 5×Paladin level, fully restored only by long rest. Ordinary spells and printed Smite fuel use the same Paladin Core V 2 RP pool; healing points never convert to RP.

Base progression is explicit rather than the ordinary 25-card template: at 1 automatically gain Lay on Hands, Divine Sense, Martial Proficiency, Divine Strike, Protective Stance and Sacred Touch. At 2 gain Righteous Challenge, Bolstering Presence, Fighting Style and ordinary Paladin spell access. At 3 swear ONE of ten Oaths; gain only its Smite modification, Aura and first Revelation spell. This Oath is the Arch specialization. At 10 enter Hero Oath Mastery of that SAME Oath; no second Oath or additional generic Hero tree. Signature Power unlocks 11, Final Gift 20. Oath Revelations automatically unlock 3/5/9/13/17, always known in addition to the shared spell repertoire, rank 1/2/3/4/5 respectively. Exact printed RP costs replace generic cost only if the card explicitly supplies them.

At 2 choose one Fighting Style: Defense +1 AC while armored; Dueling +2 damage to first one-handed melee hit on your own turn; Protection Reaction impose disadvantage on one attack against an adjacent ally when using a shield. At 3 Divine Health gives advantage on disease saves, not universal immunity. At 5 Extra Attack makes two attacks when taking the ordinary Attack Action; named attack techniques use their own counts. These three features reconcile preserved main-registry entries; other old level-table extras, including extra level 14 ASI and undefined free slot riders, are not stacked into this draft. ASI/feat at 4/8/12/16/19 follows general advancement once.

Divine Strike at 1: after one melee weapon hit on your regular turn, spend 1 RP to add S d6 radiant. At 2 this becomes Divine Smite: choose 1 RP for S d6 or 2 RP for(S+1)d8 radiant, once/own turn total. Oath 3 changes type/rider as its card states, never adds another copy of the base damage. Smite is not an ordinary spell, cannot be counterspelled or generically Overcast, and causes no Dissonance. A critical hit doubles Smite damage dice under ordinary rules, but never healing, resources or percentage copies.

One Oath aura, requires consciousness and no concentration. Radius 10 ft at 3, 15 ft at 6, 20 ft at 10, 30 ft at 15. Benefits affect up to 3 allies or 3 enemies as the Oath card states, chosen at start of your turn and changed next turn; they must stay within aura. At 6 choose one additional aura benefit for that day: allies+1 saves against fear/charm, or 1 flat DR against weapon damage. At 7 once/short rest when enemy damages an ally in aura, Reaction make one melee attack if in reach; may pay normal Smite cost even off turn, but total Smite maximum one per round from this reactive feature. At 10 aura persists until start of your next regular turn after incapacitation; then ends if still incapacitated. At 15 also grant selected allies+1 initiative while in aura when initiative is rolled; no retroactive turn changes.

At 17 Aura Surge once/short rest Bonus Action: until start next turn choose up to 3 allies in aura to gain S+M temporary HP and+1 saves. This bounded surge replaces vague doubling of every aura number. At 20 Divine Manifestation makes the aura active upon initiative without an action, radius 30 ft; it ignores ordinary Silence and terrain obstruction between allies but not antimagic explicitly suppressing divine powers, planar barriers or the consciousness rule. Source cannot-be-suppressed language is bounded explicitly. It grants no free Signature, Smite or Revelation spell.

Protected interface: Smite, Aura and Lay on Hands generate no Weave Dissonance. After a successful direct melee hit, your next Oath spell before end next turn generates 1 less Dissonance, minimum 0, consuming the benefit. No stacking, RP discount or Refrain reset. Oath Revelation spells and the five replacement Forbidden spells below are ordinary spells for strain, countering and concentration; signature powers and final gifts are Oath techniques unless expressly tagged otherwise.

Oath conduct clauses remain intact in source and Oath cards. The Director identifies a relevant clause and a knowingly chosen serious breach before applying a fall. A disagreement, failed roll, coerced act or unknown fact does not silently remove a character. A fall is an explicit story transition recorded with the player: choose the corresponding Oathbreaker inversion or pursue an agreed restoration scene. Preserve class level and already spent resources. Oathbreaker replaces its Oath Aura, Smite rider, Signature and Revelation list, rather than stacking both sets. Base martial abilities remain; Lay on Hands becomes Death Touch using the same current 5 L pool, with no refill on switching.

Death Touch baseline: Action melee divine attack PB+CHA; declare and spend 1 through 2 S+M points before the attack from remaining Lay on Hands pool to deal that much necrotic damage (choose amount before roll; miss still spends declared points). Each Oath inversion may alter type or add its bounded rider; never copy innate traits, confiscate class engines or automatically execute a target. A listed inverted Signature is available only at 11 and replaces the ordinary Signature use, one/short rest. An inverted aura follows the same radius, target cap and timing. Oathbreaker 20 uses the new Black Manifestation common capstone instead of its original Final Gift.

The source names a Forbidden Spell List but does not supply five complete entries for each inversion. This pilot explicitly adds one shared five-spell replacement list (below), with each Oathbreaker using its inversion name as flavor. These are new test rules, not recovered historical spells. Choose the normal Oath package OR inverted package at a time. All later Oath prerequisites still use Paladin class level; the Oathbreaker label does not bypass 3/11/20 gates.

Oath integration limits: one paid Smite total per round, including the level-7 Reaction; one Oath-aura reactive event per round. Multiple damage-redirection options share one event per round unless Crown Undying expressly allows two. Apply original-target defenses once, then split actual damage; transferred damage cannot be mitigated again, reflected, redirected again or generate resources. This explicit rule supersedes wording that permits recipient defenses again.

Sustained Oath spell damage/healing zones use concentration, at most three pulses, and 1 RP upkeep after the first pulse unless a priced card expressly supplies a different finite cadence. Native Oath auras retain their printed passive cadence and target cap. Final auras last their stated finite duration and include their pulses. All hard-denial effects, including compelled Actions, share the common once/source/target/encounter guard; later failures only remove Reactions and reduce Speed by half for one turn.

An emergency Reaction whose trigger itself incapacitates you, such as Grace Reversal or Thorn Crown, may resolve before that incapacitation only if you had a Reaction available before the triggering event. This grants no other actions while incapacitated. Narrative labels such as oppressor require a specific act of captivity/coercion established in the scene, not an alignment or identity assumption.

The source ceiling’s half-pool-per-round Lay on Hands cap is a preserved alternative. This pilot instead uses maximum class level per ordinary Lay on Hands Action and the explicitly once-per-long-rest level-17 Wave that distributes the current remaining pool. No normal heal gains the Wave’s exception.

For any one damage event choose exactly one Paladin redirection feature. Using it consumes the shared redirection allowance for that round. Crown Undying permits two DIFFERENT ally-damage events per round, but still only one redirection feature may modify each event.
workedExample: Paladin 5 Mercy, STR 16 CHA 16 PB 3 S 2 M 3: RP 6, Lay on Hands 25, two ordinary Attack Action attacks. Aura radius 10 ft until Paladin 6.
Turn 1 Attack Action: first hit permits 2 RP Smite, RP 6→4, adding 3d8 radiant. Second weapon hit receives no second Smite from this activation. Mercy healing uses only its printed bounded rider.
Turn 2 Action Lay on Hands spends 5 points to heal 5 HP, pool 25→20; it does not cost RP or add Dissonance. Bonus Action Protective Stance uses its own short-rest allowance; no free attack.
Turn 3 ordinary Attack Action hits. This primes the protected 1 D reduction for an Oath spell before end next turn; it does not refund 2 RP already spent or remove existing strain.

Turn 4 cast a rank 1 Oath Revelation for its printed 2 RP: RP 4→2 before strain surcharge, base 1 D becomes 0 from the primed hit. If immediately repeating the same spell, its Refrain still contributes after the single 1 D reduction.
At encounter end Lay on Hands remains 20 and RP 2. Short rest Retune restores RP by the shared formula up to 6, but never refills healing pool; long rest restores 25.
balanceQuestions: Is each Oath distinct at3 before its Signature at11?
Are Lay on Hands and RP meaningful separate budgets?
Does an Oathbreaker replacement preserve a playable character without stacking both packages?

cards.name: Aura Scaling

Choose one type of damage to gain resistance against: Fire, Necrotic, or Psychic.

Receive the ultimate blessing of your Oath, a powerful capstone ability that represents the pinnacle of your divine connection.

oathCatalog.theme: Mercy is a shelter kept open in the worst hour: protection, healing, and the preservation of life before vengeance can make another wound.
conductClauses: Never refuse a genuine plea for healing or protection when the oath can answer it
Set the saving of life before the taking of it, even when anger makes the latter easier
Offer defeated foes the mercy their surrender can bear, without abandoning those still in danger
Do not raise lethal force against the innocent or defenseless; strength was given to stand between them and harm

oathCatalog.theme: Vengeance is judgment carried through the long road: fury disciplined into pursuit, execution held to a sworn account, and no refuge promised to the unrepentant.
conductClauses: Pursue sworn enemies until justice is served or they surrender; let no convenience excuse a broken charge
Do not abandon allies to feed a private vendetta, for judgment that leaves the faithful behind is only rage
Accept the surrender of those who genuinely repent, and hold them to the peace they have asked for

oathCatalog.theme: Authority held as a public burden: law spoken plainly, judgment bound to truth, and rulership measured by the safety it keeps
conductClauses: Uphold legitimate law and order, but do not call convenience or cruelty a lawful charge
Speak truth when acting as arbiter, and hear the whole matter before you command another
Do not use authority for personal gain; a decree that serves only its speaker has already failed the oath

oathCatalog.theme: A fire kept for cleansing rather than hunger: zeal tempered by restraint, corruption confronted, and renewal guarded after the ash
conductClauses: Purify corruption and undeath where found, but name the thing being purged before you raise the flame
Do not burn the innocent in zeal; fire that cannot distinguish harm from shelter has forsaken this oath
Accept that fire renews as well as destroys, and remain to protect what must grow after the burning

oathCatalog.theme: The living memory of the old places: nature guarded as a covenant, ancient power answered with humility, and renewal left possible for those who follow
conductClauses: Protect ancient places and living memory, especially where no living voice remains to speak for them
Do not destroy what cannot be restored; power does not excuse a wound made for haste
Honor pacts with fey and primal spirits, and do not mistake an old promise for permission to command

oathCatalog.theme: Humility, watchful restraint, and strength held in quiet
conductClauses: Speak when words serve the oath; let silence bear the rest
Do not claim glory for the work entrusted to you
Hear the whole matter before you judge it

oathCatalog.theme: A vigil of iron: martyrdom, warding, and the burden freely borne for another
conductClauses: Stand between the helpless and harm, even when the cost is yours to bear
Keep every ward entrusted to you; do not abandon the bound when danger closes
Take suffering freely to spare another, but never make a chain of their sacrifice

oathCatalog.theme: Sorrow, remembrance, and the duty of passage
conductClauses: Keep faith with the dead and with those they leave behind
Do not make sport of grief or profane a place of remembrance
Guide the departed toward rest; do not claim them for undeath

oathCatalog.theme: Liberty, the breaking of unjust bonds, and freedom guarded against a new tyranny
conductClauses: Break the bonds of the unjustly imprisoned, and do not turn liberation into license to abandon them
Resist every tyrant, including the one who would rule in freedom's name
Guard the newly freed from exploitation, for an open door is not yet a safe road

oathCatalog.theme: Stewardship, the burden of the crown, and sacrifice freely borne for those in your care
conductClauses: Bear the responsibility of command without treating those in your care as a means to your glory
Set the realm's need above personal gain, and spend your own strength before you spend another's
Never demand a burden you would not freely take upon yourself

completeCurrentEnvelope.protectedInterfaceOriginal: The first cast of each different prepared Spell Matrix in an encounter generates 0 base Dissonance; repeating a matrix builds Refrain normally.
engine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Intelligence is the Wizard class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Wizard levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Intelligence modifier). Wizard spell attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier. Wizard spell save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier.

The Wizard remains three distinct stages: Base Wizard at levels 1-2, Arch Arcanist at levels 3-9, and one Hero path at levels 10-20: Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer. Hero paths are not additional starting classes and their features cannot be selected before their Wizard class-level gates.

SPELLBOOK. At Wizard 1 your spellbook contains six chosen rank-1 Wizard spells. Arcane School Specialization also adds one legal rank-1 bonus spell of your chosen school without replacing one of those six. For this provisional progression, add 2 legal Wizard spells to the book at each Wizard level 2-4, 3 at each level 5-8, 4 at each level 9-12, 5 at each level 13-16 and 6 at each level 17-20. Level-up additions cost no money or scribing time.

LEGAL RANKS. Maximum Wizard spell rank by Wizard class level is: rank 1 at levels 1-2, rank 2 at 3-4, rank 3 at 5-6, rank 4 at 7-8, rank 5 at 9-10, rank 6 at 11-12, rank 7 at 13-14, rank 8 at 15-16 and rank 9 at 17-20. Grand Tier at level 20 is a special casting permission, not a tenth ordinary rank. A Wizard may learn Wizard-list spells from any school up to the legal rank unless a spell itself has an additional prerequisite.

PREPARED SPELL MATRIX. After a long rest, prepare a number of matrices equal to Wizard level + Intelligence modifier, minimum 1, selecting only spells currently recorded in your spellbook and within your legal rank. You cast ordinary Wizard spells only from prepared matrices unless a feature explicitly overrides that restriction. Preparing the full daily matrix set normally requires 1 hour of spellbook study. Matrix Efficiency reduces this to 45 minutes.

DUPLICATE PREPARATION. You may prepare the same spell more than once, primarily to carry different Matrix Mastery configurations. Duplicate copies never create additional first-cast Dissonance exemptions. For Refrain and the protected strain rule, all prepared copies sharing the same underlying spell name belong to one matrix family regardless of modification.

MIDDAY SUBSTITUTION. Once between long rests, you may perform a 10-minute Spellbook Study ritual to replace one prepared matrix with another legal spell from your spellbook. The replacement cannot exceed your legal Wizard rank. Sigil Rewrite and Matrix Mastery may improve this process as explicitly stated.

SPELL ACQUISITION BY SCRIBING. A found Wizard spell may be copied into the spellbook if its rank is legal for you. Baseline scribing requires 2 hours and 50 gp of inks/materials per spell rank, treating rank 0 as 1 for this calculation. Spell Scribing halves both values to 1 hour and 25 gp per rank. Failure to finish the work consumes no spellbook entry but materials already expended during an interrupted hour are lost.

SPELLBOOK LOSS. Losing the spellbook does not erase matrices currently prepared in memory; you may continue casting those prepared matrices until you next rebuild or change preparation. A blank replacement book can be seeded with your currently prepared spells at 1 hour and 25 gp per effective spell rank each. An unprepared spell you previously recorded can be reconstructed from memory with 8 hours, 100 gp per rank and an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + spell rank. Failure consumes that attempt's time and half its materials; another attempt can be made after a long rest. Recovering the original book automatically restores access to its surviving entries.

ARCANE SCHOOL SPECIALIZATION is automatic at Wizard 1. Choose exactly one of the eight schools. Your spell attacks with that school gain +1 and your Wizard save DC for that school's spells gains +1. You also add one legal rank-1 spell of that school to the spellbook. The source table explicitly supplies seven school passives; the eighth core school, Abjuration, is named elsewhere but its passive row is missing. Its provisional playtest passive is identified below rather than silently presented as recovered text.

ABJURATION, provisional completion for the omitted eighth row: once per round after you cast an Abjuration spell, gain temporary HP equal to PB until the start of your next regular turn. CONJURATION: creatures summoned by your Wizard spells gain +1 maximum HP per Wizard level. DIVINATION: once per long rest reroll one failed saving throw and use the new result. ENCHANTMENT: when a creature fails its initial save against one of your Enchantment spells, a printed control duration of at least 1 round may last one additional round, but every normally allowed repeat save still occurs. EVOCATION: when casting an area Evocation spell, exclude one creature from its initial damaging area; that creature automatically succeeds and takes no damage if success normally halves damage. ILLUSION: gain +2 on concentration saves made to maintain Illusion spells. NECROMANCY: once per turn during a real encounter when a hostile non-summoned creature dies from your Necromancy spell, gain 1 temporary HP; it is not permanent healing. TRANSMUTATION: after casting a Transmutation spell, gain +5 feet Speed until the end of that turn.

PROTECTED DISSONANCE INTERFACE. The first cast of each different prepared matrix family during an encounter generates 0 BASE Dissonance. This exemption affects only base strain. Refrain and explicitly printed strain costs still apply; the suite disables generic Overcast and does not layer historical Burn onto Dissonance. Repeating a matrix family follows normal Refrain immediately. Preparing duplicates or differently modified copies of the same underlying spell never refreshes the exemption.

Core Systems V 2 Resonance Points and spell-rank RP costs are authoritative for Wizard spellcasting. There are no historical spell slots in this pilot. Wizard cards tagged wizard-spell are always-prepared class matrices once acquired, do not consume a daily prepared-matrix position and use the same RP, concentration, Refrain and protected first-distinct-matrix rules as other Wizard spells. Their printed RP cost replaces any generic rank cost; never pay both.

RITUAL CASTING is automatic at Wizard 2. A Wizard spell in your spellbook with the Ritual tag can be cast from the book without being prepared by increasing its casting time by at least 10 minutes. A ritual cast costs 0 RP unless that ritual explicitly lists a consumed RP cost, cannot be used during an encounter and cannot generate or vent Dissonance through ordinary casting strain.

Only one concentration effect can normally be maintained. Starting a second concentration effect ends the first. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; required half-damage rounding is down for this pilot. Spell Tether and the level-17 Tethered Cast are the only Wizard-specific exceptions in this draft, and each has an explicit RP price, duration and one-tether cap.

MATRIX MASTERY MODIFICATIONS. After acquiring Matrix Mastery, each prepared ordinary spell matrix may carry at most one modification chosen during preparation. QUICK SUBSTITUTION: once per short rest, replace one matrix marked Quick Substitution with another spellbook spell of exactly the same rank using a 1-minute ritual instead of the normal 10-minute midday swap; the replacement loses the modification until the next long rest. COMPONENT ENHANCEMENT: when casting a damaging or healing matrix, spend 1 additional RP to add one extra die of the spell's primary damage or healing die to one roll; if the spell has no such die this modification has no effect. MATRIX LINKING: pair two different prepared matrix families during preparation; after legally casting one, the other costs 1 less RP, minimum 1, if cast before the end of your next regular turn, at most once per pair per round. STABILITY REINFORCEMENT: gain +2 on concentration saves caused by damage while maintaining that matrix. A matrix modification never creates another spell cast or proc event.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant another additional Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Spell copies, Matrix Sharing, Arcane Fusion, Dual Cast and similar effects pay all explicitly required RP and do not produce duplicate resource, cast-proc or action-grant chains beyond their written resolution.

Round recharge counters decrease once at the start of your regular initiative turn even if you cannot act. Extra Actions and extra turns do not tick recharge. Outside initiative, each uninterrupted 6 seconds counts as one tick. Only positive counters can be reset or shortened and each named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

SUMMON COMMAND LIMIT. All Wizard-controlled conjured, raised and bound companions share one damaging/control Companion Command per Wizard regular turn. Spend one Bonus Action to command exactly one such creature to move up to its Speed and use one damaging or control action from its stat block. Uncommanded creatures may reposition defensively and take Dodge but cannot deal damage or impose conditions. No summoned or raised creature can create XP, treasure, RP, Dissonance relief, additional corpses or kill-resource farms.

NECROMANCER STANDARD UNDEAD. Corpse Harvest and Auto-Raise share a maximum of three standard raised minions. Skeleton: AC 14, HP 6 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Bone Shot, range 30 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. Zombie: AC 12, HP 10 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 20; Slam, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. Goblin Thrall, available only from a goblinoid corpse: AC 13, HP 8 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Shiv, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. These are pre-Flesh-Ascendant statistics.

NECROMANCER AUTO-RAISE. Once per round when one of your standard undead minions personally lands the killing blow on an eligible humanoid and your standard-minion count is below three, its corpse rises at the end of the current turn as the same mechanical minion type that scored the kill, if physically possible. A new minion cannot act during that same round. Auto-Raise costs no Action or RP but can never exceed the three-minion cap or generate a new resource, corpse chain, XP or treasure event. Without Infernal Pact only humanoids qualify.

ELITE UNDEAD PETS. Necromancers may bind Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound, at most one of each and three elite pets total. They use the same shared Companion Command limit as standard undead. Boneflayer: AC 14, HP 12 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Bone Shards: range 60, Wizard spell attack, 2d6+S necrotic. Fear Pulse replaces its attack: enemies within 10 feet make Wisdom saves; failure Frightened until end of next turn; recharge 3. Grave Miasma replaces its attack: 10-foot-radius point within 30 feet until start of your next turn; enemies entering or starting there take 1d6 necrotic once; recharge 3.

Dreadblade: AC 16, HP 16 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Disrupting Blade: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic; a concentrating target immediately makes its concentration save with disadvantage. On a natural 20 the target is Weakened until the end of its next turn, taking -1 on attack rolls. Dreadblade has advantage on saves against forced movement.

Wraithbound: AC 14, HP 10 + 2 × Wizard level, Fly 40 and hover. While it has not attacked or imposed control since the end of its previous turn it is Invisible; attacking ends that state until the end of its next turn. Wraith Strike: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. On natural 20 the target makes a Constitution save against your Wizard DC; failure Stuns until the end of its next turn.

Flesh Ascendant's bonus applies after the listed base statistics: every undead creature you control gains +2 maximum HP per Wizard level. If at least two of your undead creatures are active, each gains +1 AC and +1 on saving throws. This does not increase the standard-minion or elite-pet caps.

DARK-TRAUMA INTERFACE. Necromancer features involving corpse desecration, infernal bargains, domination, body control or Mind Prison remain subject to the project's existing dark-content and trauma boundaries. A table may fade description to black without changing mechanics. No feature changes a player's real belief, permanently transfers ownership of a player character or silently retires a PC.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Wizard 1 automatically gains Arcane School Specialization, Spell Matrix System and the starting spellbook, then chooses 4 selectable Base cards, at least 2 Active. Wizard 2 automatically gains Counterspell and Ritual Casting, then chooses 2 additional selectable Base cards. Counterspell is not also placed in the Arch selection pool.

At Wizard 3 enter Arcanist, automatically gain Arcane Tradition as an upgrade of the SAME level-1 school rather than choosing another school, and choose 2 selectable Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Wizard 4 grants one eligible Base/Arch choice. Wizard 5 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic School Mastery. Wizard 6 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic Arcane Ward. Wizard 7 grants one eligible Arch choice. Wizard 8 grants one Base/Arch choice. Wizard 9 grants one eligible Arch choice plus automatic Dual Cast.

At Wizard 10 choose Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer and gain 2 Hero cards from that path. ELEMENTALIST EXCEPTION: Elemental Affinity is automatic at path selection and counts as one of those two level-10 Hero acquisitions, so an Elementalist chooses only one additional Hero card at level 10. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. The chosen Final Theorem is automatic at Wizard 20. School Mastery, Counterspell, Arcane Tradition and all progression-table automatic features are never duplicated as selections.

All acquisition gates use Wizard class level rather than total character level. Normal proficiency bonus follows the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. A multiclass dip cannot unlock higher spell ranks, Arcanist cards, Hero cards, Final Theorems or progression-table features.

Class matrices tagged wizard-spell receive a rank in normalized card data equal to maximum ordinary Wizard rank at their minimum class-level gate (cap 9). Printed RP cost replaces generic rank cost. Counterspell is rank 1 at its explicit level 2 automatic grant. This explicit convention closes rank-dependent Counterspell/Dissonance interactions without inventing extra costs.

Cantrip completion: know 3 Wizard cantrips at 1, 4 at 4, 5 at 10, using the shared missing-repertoire fallback. Cantrips are known directly and do not consume prepared matrices. Always-prepared class matrices are additional cards, not extra arbitrary ordinary spells. Class spell ranks and the normalized activation field resolve incomplete source terminology.
workedExample: Wizard 9 example: Intelligence 16 gives M=3, PB=4 and S=2. Assume the authoritative Core V 2 sheet gives this Wizard 32 RP. The Wizard has prepared Fireball, Web, Shield and other matrices; has selected Spell Efficiency; and begins a real encounter with Dissonance 3.

Turn 1: cast prepared Fireball for its normal rank-3 Core V 2 cost of 5 RP, so RP 32→27. This is the first Fireball matrix-family cast of the encounter, so its BASE casting strain produces 0 Dissonance. Any independent Overcast or other risk would still apply, but none is used here.

Turn 2: cast Fireball again. Spell Efficiency reduces the repeat by 1 RP, minimum 1, so this cast costs 4 RP and RP 27→23. Because Fireball has already received its first-distinct exemption, normal Refrain applies to this repeat; the protected interface does not suppress that Refrain.

Enemy turn: an enemy begins a rank-3 spell. Counterspell costs 3 RP, so RP 23→20. The Wizard rolls Intelligence + proficiency against DC 16 under the pilot Counterspell card. Counterspell is a different always-prepared class matrix, so its first cast receives the base-strain exemption; success negates the triggering spell after its costs are paid.

Turn 3: use the automatic level-9 Dual Cast, which is available once per short rest. Cast two DIFFERENT prepared spells of rank 1 or 2 as one Action sequence, paying both costs. If they cost 2 RP and 3 RP, RP 20→15. Each underlying matrix independently checks first-cast/Refrain state, but cast-trigger effects that say 'once per turn' still trigger only once as written.

Turn 4: cast one member of a Matrix-Linked pair for 3 RP, RP 15→12. Before the end of the next regular turn the paired matrix qualifies for its 1-RP reduction. If that paired spell normally costs 3 RP, its linked cast costs 2 RP, RP 12→10. The link changes cost only; it creates no additional spell, Action or Dissonance exemption.
balanceQuestions: Does preparing Wizard level + Intelligence modifier matrices, while also learning the historically broad number of spellbook entries, create meaningful daily planning without making spellbook management too burdensome at high level?

Do Matrix Mastery, Dual Cast, Spell Efficiency, Arcane Fusion and Tethered Cast preserve the Wizard's methodical identity without producing excessive RP efficiency, concentration bypass or cast-proc multiplication?
Are Spellbinder suppression, Elementalist combination effects and Necromancer minion control comparably valuable when tested across several encounters with the same Core V2 RP and rest schedule?

This is RP recovery, not a second pool, and cannot trigger spell-cast, Refrain or Dissonance effects.

cards.rangeAndTarget: Your spellbook
cards.effect: Spell Scribing. Tags: base, passive, spellbook. Copying a legal found Wizard spell into your spellbook requires 1 hour and 25 gp of inks and components per spell rank, treating rank 0 as rank 1 for this calculation, instead of the pilot baseline 2 hours and 50 gp. Level-up spells remain free.

source.originalText: Spell Scribing: Copy spells into your spellbook at half the normal cost and time.

cards.name: Arcane Insight
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self
cards.effect: Arcane Insight. Tags: base, passive, knowledge. Gain proficiency in Arcana, or expertise if already proficient. The Director sets the normal knowledge DC; failure supplies no invented fact.

It does not grant advantage on spell attacks, Counterspell checks or general Investigation unrelated to arcane scholarship.

source.originalText: Scholarly Mind: Gain advantage on Intelligence checks related to arcane knowledge.

cards.name: Arcane Bolt
cards.rangeAndTarget: One creature within 60 feet
cards.effect: Arcane Bolt. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, universal, damage. Make a Wizard spell attack. On a hit deal S d6 + M force damage. Arcane Bolt is an always-prepared class matrix once acquired and uses the normal first-distinct-matrix and Refrain rules.

cards.name: Minor Conjuration
