DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/me.fullCurrentText:
# Shared rules for the class playtest drafts

**Provisional design integration, 8 October 2026.** These rules make the class drafts usable together for testing. They preserve each protected class engine while specifying missing timing and replacing conflicting old percentages. They do not rewrite the approved Word books. Original descriptions and alternate registry entries remain in `data/playtest/class_sources`.

## Reading a class card

Use the class's own level, never total character level, for gates and effects. **L** means that class level; **S** is 1/2/3/4 at class levels 1/5/11/17. **M** means max(1, the class ability modifier), for effect a mounts only. Attacks use d20 + normal character proficiency + the actual appropriate ability modifier. Class save DC is 8 + normal proficiency + actual class ability modifier. Negative modifiers still apply to attacks and DCs. One tile is 5 ft. Fractions round down unless specified. Distances cannot be negative.

A weapon attack uses its usual ability, weapon die and damage type. A technique that says “make one weapon attack” replaces your Action with that attack; it does not also grant a normal Attack Action or Extra Attack. Generic attack-speed language has no effect beyond the exact attacks printed in the draft. A spell attack uses the class's stated casting ability. Natural 1 misses and natural 20 hits/critically doubles damage dice; flat bonuses do not double. A save succeeds at DC; “fails by 10” means the total is at least 10 below DC. Critical-range improvements never stack; use the broadest one.

An ability is known only if granted or selected by the draft schedule. Satisfy all printed prerequisites, target legality, action availability, recharge and resource costs before spending anything. A failed legal attack/save attempt still pays; an illegal activation spends nothing. No resource goes below 0 or above its cap. A class feature name shared with a spell does not grant both versions; use the version selected, with its own cost and timing. Names and source text are preserved; the current card is the operational draft.

## Action and timing limits

One regular Action, one Bonus Action if a feature permits it, normal movement and one Reaction between starts of your turns. A free trigger costs no Action only if expressly stated. All grants share **one extra full Action per creature per round**. An extra Action cannot grant another Action, recharge itself, or start another extra-Action grant. It supplies no extra Bonus Action or Reaction. A card granting additional attacks is not permission to repeat all class riders on every hit: obey each rider's frequency.

Recharge N sets a counter to N after use; reduce once at the start of the owner's regular initiative turn, whether able to act or not. Extra turns/Actions do not tick it. Outside combat tick once per 6 elapsed seconds, without double counting. Recharge 2 used on turn 1 is ready on turn 3. A positive counter can be reset/shortened at most once per ability per round. Zero counters are not legal reset targets and expend no reset use. Resets never restore RP or per-rest uses or grant an immediate activation.

An encounter is a genuine scene of uncertain opposition chosen by the Director, not a player declaration used to reset resources. No encounter gain from attacking allies, one's summons, harmless animals, helpless captives or reused corpses. Out-of-combat abilities retain all printed costs and time. Short-rest means a completed uninterrupted hour of permitted recovery; long-rest means a completed 8-hour Rest Watch. This time convention is a draft integration. Expedition pressure, supplies, safe locations and rest debt still matter. A long rest also refreshes short-rest uses; a short rest never refreshes long-rest uses. Weekly uses refresh after seven full in-world days, not repeated rests.

## Targets, concentration and control

Unless expressly stated, perceive the target, remain within range and have line of effect; total cover blocks targeting. “Ally” includes self unless it says OTHER. A list cannot contain a creature twice. Select up to the printed limit; an empty target list is not a valid way to farm activation benefits. Zones remain at their chosen point unless described as an aura; allies can leave and lose their benefits. An aura requires its owner conscious unless the card supplies a bounded exception. An effect ending at “end next turn” means the affected creature's next turn only when the card says target's; otherwise the user's.

One concentration slot for all spells, Chants, Veinweaves, forms or zones that require concentration. Starting another ends the old before the new effect resolves, except for an explicit limited linked-effect rule. Damage prompts CON save against max(10, floor(damage/2)); incapacitation or a failed save ends concentration. The round-down convention is a deliberate pilot interpretation. Concentration does not demand a Bonus Action unless maintenance says so. For a paid 3-pulse effect, start is pulse 1; pay maintenance on each of the next 2 regular turns by turn end for pulses 2/3. Missing payment ends it at that turn's end; otherwise it ends at start of turn 4. No repeated start triggers on maintenance.

Forced movement does not provoke opportunity attacks unless explicitly stated, cannot place a creature inside solid matter, and stops at an obstacle. Grapples use the card's save/DC, can be escaped with an Action and STR(Athletics) or DEX(Acrobatics) against that DC, and end beyond reach. A root sets Speed 0 but does not remove Actions. Slows reduce Speed to minimum 0. Silence blocks verbal spells/audible abilities, not all thought or all class features. Charmed effects never determine a player's beliefs; use only the printed action restrictions.

No repeated hard denial without a new save and cost. For this class suite, a creature can suffer **Stunned, compelled loss of its whole Action/turn, or equivalent hard denial from a given character at most once per encounter**, across that character's class features; later such riders fail while damage and soft riders resolve normally. Record source and target. This draft guard is broader than the older Oracle-only ceiling and is an explicit balance proposal. Reaction denial, Speed reduction, penalties and Frightened do not count as whole-turn loss. Do not silently waive boss immunities, legendary defenses or anatomy.

## Damage, healing, stacking and companions

Roll once for each shared area/pulse and apply saves/defenses to each target separately; separate attacks roll separately. Halve once for a successful save and apply resistance/immunity normally. Same-named conditions/bonuses do not stack unless a printed cap allows it; same-stat flat bonuses from these class techniques use the strongest. Different resources remain separate. Damage reduction from these class features uses the strongest flat reduction, then applies resistance; it cannot create negative damage or healing. Temporary HP never stack; choose the larger remaining amount. Immunity is not reduced resistance.

Repeated permanent HP recovery must consume finite RP, a per-rest use or another finite resource; a combat-generated gauge alone never enables unlimited healing. Healing cannot exceed maximum HP or erase Wounds, death consequences, debt or Corruption unless explicit. Downed is living at 0 HP; dead is different. Resurrection requires a willing soul and sufficiently intact body, obeys its time window, cannot create a duplicate and never refunds the feature on failure to meet known prerequisites. Sacrificial HP is actual unpreventable loss, cannot be redirected or paid with temporary HP, and is not damage for resource triggers. It cannot reduce the donor below 1 unless a card expressly grants a death-triggered effect.

No damage/healing copy repeats the source's costs, procs, resource generation, critical bonus dice, buffs, actions, cooldown resets or duration. Compute fractions once, capped at 100% of one stored source unless an explicit card states a separately priced higher amount. Copies still cause ordinary damage consequences, concentration checks and death. A copy cannot copy another copy. A target/source record must refer to an actual resolved event, not merely a known ability name.

Where a class card calls for a **standard companion** without a more specific profile, use: Small or Medium; AC 12+floor(PB/2); HP 2 L; walking Speed 30 ft; saves equal owner's PB; one melee or ranged attack (reach 5 ft/range 30 ft) at owner's class attack bonus, damage S d6 of the printed type. It has no independent class features, resources, loot, death triggers or extra turns. All companions belonging to one character share one Bonus Action command and **one damaging attack/action total per round** unless a specifically priced feature grants more. Without a command they move and Dodge. Act immediately after owner. A standard companion lasts 1 minute, disappears at 0 HP and cannot be healed for free by dismissing/resummoning. The creation cost must be paid again. Creature-specific stat blocks override this profile only where explicitly printed.

## Ordinary spells: one explicit test configuration

Use the manifest-owned **Core Systems Known Descent V 2** class RP tables and rank costs: rank 0–9 costs 0/2/3/5/7/10/13/17/21/26; Grand 32. Follow `src/data/class-spell-progression.js` for each class's rank gates and the existing spell catalog for class/school access. Having enough RP never bypasses a rank gate. Oracle has Revelation Charges, and Soldier/Warrior have no general RP spellcasting. Multiclass spell access is determined separately per class; do not add complete class pools or use total level to unlock a rank. This suite's printed pool tables are single-class; use the existing multiclass pool formula with the new constituent Core V 2 pools for mixed characters.

Four classes have no direct Core V 2 pool row. For this pilot, Crimson Agent uses the Cleric curve multiplied by 0.5; Dragoon, Monk and Thief use that curve multiplied by 0.35, rounded to nearest integer with halves upward, minimum 1. These fallback factors come from the preserved `src/data/resonance-economy.js`; they are explicitly distinguished from direct book tables. The generic Core V 2 Oracle RP row is rejected for this class suite because Oracle's protected class contract uses Revelation Charges only. Oracle never receives RP or ordinary spell access. Retune here means one recovery at the end of a completed short rest, not an unrestricted action.

For a reproducible pilot, retain the protected **Dissonance** layer with Core V 2 numeric RP costs. This combination is a new integration decision: do not also roll a second historical Burn/fizzle system on top of it. Limit=max(4, 2+PB+max(0, casting modifier)). Before a ranked cast, Dissonance at limit/limit+3/limit+6 adds 1/2/3 RP respectively; at limit+6 ordinary casters cannot cast rank 1+. At limit+3 ordinary Overcast is unavailable. A cast then adds base Dissonance 0 at rank 0, 1 at ranks 1–5, 2 at ranks 6–9. Immediate repeated casts of the same named spell add 1, 2, then 3 maximum. Another named spell resets the repeat counter but not accumulated strain. Apply the class's exact cadence reduction/vent; never infer a free RP reduction. Printed class techniques pay printed costs and cause no automatic spell Dissonance unless tagged or expressly described as spells, Echo releases or Matrix casts. For a Mage/Wizard class card tagged as a spell, use the rank printed in normalized data; its rank is fixed at acquisition and does not rise with S. Other techniques are not counterspell able unless their card says so.

Retune recovers max(0, round(max RP/4)+casting modifier), never above maximum, and clears Dissonance. A long rest restores RP and clears Dissonance. Optional 10-minute meditation once/day recovers positive casting modifier RP and reduces Dissonance by PB+positive modifier. A regular turn with no spell or magical class ability loses 1 Dissonance; an Action spent Grounding without casting loses PB instead (not both). Merely ending an encounter does not clear accumulated Dissonance. Refrain survives idle/weapon turns unless a class explicitly clears it. Lich/Necromancer may force ranked casts through Fracture; after resolution take direct unpreventable trauma equal to rank×1/2/3 at the three strained states, minimum 1, based on state before casting. This trauma cannot generate resources or trigger damage-sharing. They still pay RP and meet rank gates.

Generic Overcast is excluded from the initial suite configuration until its options are separately fixed; cards such as Overchannel have their own exact costs and gates. Core V 2's original Burn procedures, older rank×2 costs and smaller companion RP tables remain preserved as alternatives, not silently combined. This configuration is suit able for comparing class drafts, not a claim that all historical magic sources already agree.

## Spell repertoires and acquisition

Preserve explicit class spellbook/preparation rules where given. For classes missing a known-spell count, this suite proposes: full casters know 3 cantrips at 1, 4 at 4, 5 at 10 and choose 2 ranked spells at first spell access plus 1 each later class level; hybrid/half/minor casters know 2 cantrips at first cantrip access and 3 at class 10, and choose 2 ranked spells at first ranked access plus 1 on each later even class level. At a long rest, a known caster may replace one known spell with a legal same-or-lower rank selection. This fills an actual missing rule and does not replace a more specific Druid prepared list or Wizard spellbook. Bonus spells expressly granted by a class are additional. No unnamed or mechanically unfinished catalog spell becomes complete merely by entering this repertoire; select operational spells for the test and record them.

Scheduled selection applies only where the class document says so. At each milestone choose distinct eligible entries; no banked Skill Points. Automatic engines, ASIs, feats, forms and finales do not also consume a choice unless stated. Ordinary-class schedule:4 Base at 1 (at least 2 active), 2 Base at 2; 2 Arch at 3 (at least 1 active); alternating 1 Base/Arch at 4/6/8/11/13/15/17/19 and 1 Arch at 5/7/9; choose Hero at 10 and 2 Hero (at least 1 active), then 1 Hero at 12/14/16/18; finale 20. If a class has no source Arch capstone, level 9 has the printed class-specific grant or another choice, explicitly shown. The individual schedule and prerequisite checks win over this summary. ASI or eligible feat at 4/8/12/16/19, separate from choices, except Oracle uses its explicit 4/8/14/19 schedule. Druid, Oracle and Paladin use their own schedules.

## Shared interpretation

**family.bleeding.** Explicit hostile Bleed classification for immunity, curing and stated eligibility. Class/owner/source timing and caps remain separate. No inherited damage package.

**family.ongoing-fire.** Only explicitly registered creature-attached Burn-style periodic fire. Excludes direct fire, areas, hazards, environmental flames, object ignition, Resonance Burn and names alone.

**periodic.arbitration.** Generic Core and custom groups enter ONE family arbitration at an identical target marker. Within each family at one identical target timing marker, select one stack group by highest expected unmitigated damage then earliest application. Apply source instance caps before comparing. All due groups consume their tick, including non-damaging losers. Different markers and families resolve separately. Stable unique application sequence breaks simultaneous applications in resolution order; lexical group ID is a final implementation tie-break only.

**ownership.** Ordinary your means ownerCharacterId. Explicit class phrases restrict sourceClass. Crimson technical Bleed engine hooks require owned Crimson instances. Suppressed, immune, inactive or expired effects do not satisfy active-effect hooks.

**hp-cure-separation.** HP prohibition prevents regained HP. Legal positive-potential magical healing can still invoke a registered Bleed cure, including Blood Curse CON save; a remover explicitly requiring actual HP gained retains that prerequisite.

**exclusive-periodic-binding.** A textual effect component with a reviewed source-qualified profile creates only that record. Core Bleeding/Burning are fallback identities only for explicit Core applications lacking a more-specific profile. A family tag or display word never also creates a generic record. Two records require two effects explicitly imposed by the operative source.

**immunity-and-periodic-arbitration.** Condition/family immunity prevents initial application. Gained condition/family immunity suppresses an existing record: clocks and due ticks continue, but suppressed records are excluded from damage arbitration and active-effect hooks. Damage-type immunity/resistance does not suppress the record or exclude it from arbitration; choose using unmitigated expectation, then apply defenses.

**recipe-occupancy.** A poison recipe occupies an ongoing-instance slot only while at least one ongoing component remains. Suppression does not erase an existing component; curing/expiry can end it. Resolved one-time critical healing does not occupy a slot. Ending Bloodleech's sole remaining Bleed ends its occupancy without purging other poison or curse records.

**cure-presence-suppression.** SUPERSESSION: Cure/removal tests existing unexpired presence, not current effect activity. Medicine selects one present eligible Bleed; positive-potential legal magical healing invokes each present eligible endpoint (Blood Curse retains CON save); Action/full immersion ends all present ordinary-extinguishable fires. Suppression/acquired condition immunity does not bar these cures or existing permitted ending saves. Damage arbitration and active-effect hooks still exclude suppressed/immune records. Initial immunity prevents new application; ended records cannot resume.

**Application records.** Preserve application ID, owner character, source class/engine, target, DC, damage type, start, remaining ticks or expiry, source stack group, and cure exceptions. “Immune” in an active-effect eligibility check means immunity to the condition/application, not merely immunity to its damage type. Damage immunity does not by itself erase an effect.

**Timing.** Explicit start/end timing wins. An omitted next-turn periodic marker is provisionally end of the next regular target turn. Extra turns add no periodic ticks or ending saves. Outside initiative preserve the clock and consume one due step per complete six seconds; initiative transitions do not duplicate events.

**Bleed treatment.** A WIS (Medicine) Action by self or an adjacent helper selects one ordinary Bleed record before rolling: printed cure DC, otherwise recorded applying effect/class/spell DC, otherwise 10. Success ends that record. One legal magical-healing event with positive pre-cap/pre-prohibition potential ends every eligible automatic-healing-cure record; each Blood Curse instead receives its own CON save. An explicit remover keeps its stated one/all/owner scope.

**Cure presence.** Treatment, magical-healing cure and permitted per-record ending saves can remove a still-present suppressed or condition-immune Bleed/fire record. Cure scope and special prerequisites remain unchanged. Effect eligibility and damage arbitration still exclude suppressed records. Successful removal ends the record permanently; immunity ending cannot restore it.

**Kit exceptions.** A Crimson kit Action consumes one use and ends that source owner's Crimson Bleeds on the victim. A Dragoon kit Action consumes one use and ends the selected Dragoon Bleed. Other records do not silently acquire these kit endpoints.

**Attached fire treatment.** One self/helper extinguish Action or full immersion ends all ordinary-extinguishable attached fires on that creature. Explicit protected-fire exceptions survive. At the end of each regular target turn, after due ticks are consumed, each still-active fire record with future ticks remaining receives its own ending DEX save at its source DC or 10. An indefinite generic fire has future ticks. No ending save is needed after a record's final tick expires.

**Duration changes.** Printed base duration is distinct from an express hard cap. A qualifying refresh never shortens remaining duration. Persistent Bleed normally supplies two turns; Prolonged Suffering changes application/refresh to four only for owned profiles whose printed base is exactly two. Use the greatest legal replacement, not a sum; obey actual hard caps. No source trigger means no refresh, and expired records cannot be refreshed.

# Condition recovery and exposure — provisional procedures

**Reviewed provisional integration, 8 October 2026.** These are fictional game procedures. The sources provide the condition identities, existing dose/tolerance rules, six Exhaustion levels and Intoxication thresholds; the exact generic recovery projects and missing endpoints below are newly authored proposals discussed with GPT. Preserve the original sources. Use with [all 28 conditions](CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md) and [HP, Wounds and death](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md).

## Time, costs and checks

A project day is a consecutive 24-hour interval starting when that project begins, not a calendar-date change. A three-day project finishes no earlier than 72 elapsed hours; seven days means at least 168 hours. Only one project of the same kind for the same patient and named condition may be active. Concurrent clocks measure the same elapsed time once; the same active hour or consumed Supply cannot pay two activities. An active practitioner cannot simultaneously perform a long rest. A patient can receive care while resting where the care permits it.

Consume each stated Supply or kit use at the beginning of its attempt or daily work. Interruption does not refund it. Missing a required project day, taking a forbidden dose or receiving forbidden new Exposure ends that attempt; completed costs remain spent, and starting again requires a fresh full project. Merely suppressing symptoms does not interrupt abstinence or time already properly completed.

Project skill checks use the reviewed four-degree task rules. Success and Critical Success give the stated success; Failure and Critical Failure give the stated failure unless specifically differentiated. No extra reward or complication is inferred from an undefined degree. Saving throws remain binary. Use WIS (Medicine), INT (Religion), INT (Arcana), or an INT check using proficiency with alchemist's supplies for Alchemy. These ability/tool assignments are explicit integration choices; an actual feature can supply its printed alternative.

## Exhaustion

The six V6 effects are cumulative: level 1 disadvantage on ability checks; 2 Speed halved; 3 disadvantage on attack rolls and saves; 4 maximum HP halved; 5 Speed zero; 6 death. Compute level-4 maximum as `max(1, floor(otherwise-applicable maximum HP / 2))`. Recompute from the otherwise-applicable maximum whenever it changes. Clamp current HP when the maximum falls; restoring the maximum does not heal. Flat Speed changes apply before halving; a zero-Speed condition overrides the calculation. A maximum-HP reduction alone is not damage and does not trigger a Wound save.

**NEW generic recovery:** At the end of a beneficial eight-hour long rest, remove one Exhaustion level from a living creature at levels 1–5 if it met the campaign's food/water requirements, the originating cause no longer actively imposes or refreshes Exhaustion, and no source-specific rule blocks removal of the chosen level. At most one generic level can be removed per 24 elapsed hours. Specific reviewed effects can remove additional levels as printed. A prerequisite such as Moisture Dependency's one-hour immersion unlocks recovery; it does not itself remove a level unless explicitly stated. Track blocked-source levels separately so another source's removable level may still be selected; the patient chooses a legal level to remove.

Exhaustion 6 causes death. Removing levels from the corpse never revives it. A resurrection effect must also leave the creature below 6 or it immediately dies again. Global Exhaustion, expedition Strain, Warrior serum Strain and Oracle's one-turn Revelation backlash remain separate records; this procedure clears none of those other tracks. See the [Strain namespace candidate](STRAIN_PLAYTEST.md) for its separately recorded review status.

## Dependence and Withdrawal

Preserve Core's existing substance procedures: resolve benefit and crash; a repeat dose before the next long rest requires the substance's dependence CON save; three uses within seven days cause tolerance that halves duration unless doubled; more than two doses before a long rest triggers the substance's severe complication and dependence advancement. This document supplies endpoints, not a replacement substance catalog. Use each item's reviewed dependence DC and severe complication. An item lacking its actual consequence remains in the item review queue rather than gaining an invented generic overdose result.

**Maintenance:** At each completed long rest, a new maintenance dose is due for each named dependence. Withdrawal applies immediately until a qualifying dose is taken after that rest; a dose taken before its completion cannot satisfy the new interval. The dose ends that substance's current symptoms until the next maintenance interval but does not remove dependence. Ordinary consumption time, stock, crash, tolerance and repeated-dose rules still apply. No free dose or Action is granted.

**Tolerance:** Record doses in a rolling seven-day window. After the third completed dose/use within that window, tolerance becomes active; subsequent uses have half duration unless doubled. The third ordinary use is not retroactively shortened. Count a doubled dose as two doses for tolerance, repeated-dose and overdose accounting; resolve its two-dose thresholds as one consumption event, with at most one dependence save for that event. Seven full days with no dose clears tolerance. One long rest does not clear tolerance. Track each substance separately.

**NEW dependence recovery project:** Complete seven consecutive project days without a dose of the named substance. Each day the patient spends one hour in treatment/recovery work and consumes one Supply. Choose Medicine, Religion or Alchemy at project start. At the end of the seventh full day, the designated practitioner (who may be the patient) makes that check against the substance's dependence DC, or NEW DC 14 if a direct Addicted effect supplied no substance DC. Success removes that named Addicted and its associated Withdrawal. Failure removes neither; a new attempt needs a new seven-day project. There is no extra automatic Wound on Critical Failure.

The existing Haven activity “Treat Dependence or Withdrawal” gives advantage on the next recovery check and prevents one ordinary withdrawal escalation after one full day under qualified care. For this bridge, a proficient practitioner spends an eight-hour care activity during a project day; that day's one-hour treatment requirement is included, not additional. Advantage applies once to the next recovery check and cannot be stockpiled. Different sources of advantage still do not stack. The activity does not independently cure dependence or erase a dose's printed crash.

Withdrawal imposes disadvantage on ability checks. “Disadvantage on RP recovery” affects an actual RP recovery roll only; deterministic Retune receives no invented arithmetic penalty. Oracle RC is not RP. The generic Withdrawal condition has no further severity track. An individual substance can add an explicitly reviewed duration or escalation; otherwise do not invent one. Symptom-removal magic does not remove dependence unless it explicitly does, but valid symptom suppression is compatible with completing a no-dose project.

## Intoxication

Use one dose-driven score from 0 to 5. Increase it only when an effect explicitly grants Intoxication. A direct effect saying “Intoxicated” supplies a minimum effective score of 2 for its printed duration, or NEW two hours when no duration is supplied. It does not add dose-driven points or count as a dose. Effective score is the greater of the dose-driven score and the active generic floor of 2. Generic timed floors of 3–5 do not exist. A source explicitly setting level 3–5 must individually define its dose-driven change or its own complete recovery exception before becoming operational. Each no-duration floor-2 application expires exactly two elapsed hours after application. Multiple direct floors do not stack, but the floor persists while any is active. Removing one leaves independent points and other direct applications intact.

| Score | Consequence |
|---|---|
| 0 | Sober; no Intoxication consequence. |
| 1 | Disadvantage on precise-memory checks. One available advantage use on a fear save. |
| 2 | Also disadvantage on precise DEX and INT checks. |
| 3 | Also Dazed and Speed −10 feet. |
| 4 | Also Unconscious for the level-4 timer and a poisoning save. |
| 5 | Also a medical emergency with a fixed one-hour deadline. |

The rows are cumulative. The Director identifies a “precise” check before rolling: fine manipulation or exact memory/analysis, not every possible use of DEX/INT. The player may spend the one fear-save advantage use before rolling. It refreshes only after effective score reaches 0 and a later new episode begins, never at each positive level. An explicit independent Dazed, Unconscious or Poisoned effect is not removed merely because intoxication ends.

**NEW natural reduction:** At dose-driven scores 1–3, one complete hour without new Intoxication removes one point; repeat each hour. A new positive gain resets that hourly timer even if a direct floor conceals the dose-driven change. A timed floor itself does not stop underlying points declining. At score 4 use its specific timer; score 5 cannot decay naturally. After a reduction to 3 or below, begin the next hourly interval at that transition. A timed floor can prevent the effective score from dropping until that application ends.

**NEW level 4:** On entering effective score 4 (or returning from treated 5), roll 1d4 once and set that many hours as the recovery deadline. Make a DC 14 CON save; on failure add Poisoned caused by intoxication while effective score is at least 4. Unconscious from this track lasts until that deadline unless cured earlier. Ending Unconscious alone does not clear points or reset the deadline. Reapplying score 4 without leaving it does not reroll or extend the deadline. At its deadline, if alive and no emergency is active, reduce dose-driven score to at most 3 and end track-caused Unconscious/Poisoned. A generic cure explicitly ending Intoxication removes all its track/floor records and track-caused consequences.

**NEW level 5:** On entering score 5, set a fixed emergency deadline one hour later and become/remain Unconscious. A jump directly from below 4 to 5 starts the emergency immediately; the level-4 recovery timer and poisoning save begin only after successful care returns it to 4. Additional gains at 5 never reset or extend it. A helper may spend ten uninterrupted minutes and one healer's-kit use, consumed at start, then make DC 15 WIS (Medicine). Success before the deadline ends the emergency, sets the dose-driven score to 4, adds one Wound if below three, and begins the level-4 timer/save. At three Wounds, successful emergency care prevents death without creating a fourth Wound; this is a specific provisional exception for this treatment. This direct Wound has no Injury roll and does not itself trigger a Wound save. Wound immunity prevents that added Wound where applicable.

Failure leaves the original emergency and deadline; another fully paid attempt is possible if it can finish before that deadline. At the exact deadline, death takes precedence over an unfinished or simultaneously finishing generic attempt. No natural score reduction can clear the emergency. A reviewed effect explicitly removing Intoxication or the emergency can end it by its own procedure. An immunity to Unconscious or Poisoned does not, by itself, prevent the separate emergency or death state.

## Corrupted

Use the condition's half healing, individually recorded Evil-source save disadvantage, aura and DC 15 WIS long-rest save. A failed long-rest save shifts the moral axis Good → Neutral → Evil without changing law/chaos. Never infer Evil from ancestry, species, faction, homeland or appearance. This label change does not compel beliefs, behavior, PvP, party separation or automatic oathbreaking. Specific conduct clauses still judge actual conduct.

**NEW generic cleansing:** One practitioner spends eight uninterrupted hours with one patient in a secure location, consumes one Supply at start, and makes INT (Religion) or INT (Arcana) against DC 15 at completion. Success removes Corrupted. Failure leaves it without any extra automatic Wound, condition or Exposure. No more than one generic attempt may complete for that patient in 24 elapsed hours; practitioners cannot stack concurrent attempts. The practitioner is working, while the patient may rest if otherwise eligible. If cleansing and the patient's long rest complete together, resolve cleansing first; make the Corrupted rest save only if it remains. A specific reviewed cleansing spell/item uses its own costs and procedure.

Guaranteed one-HP recovery from a natural-20 death save or the Stable recovery clock remains one HP: these are state-recovery rules, not healing effects. Ordinary one-point magical healing can still be halved to zero. It nevertheless ends generic Bleeding if it had positive pre-reduction healing potential.

## Unity Exposure — public provisional track

The source defines a 0–6 track with erosion of distinction and identity but no operational numeric threshold table was found in the bounded Core/V6/Director and current reference searches. GPT also reported no owner-approved numerical table in its available notebook history. The following is **NEW candidate mechanics**, not recovered setting truth. It grants no public knowledge of the exposure's hidden causes or identities.

Use the current row only; do not add lower-row modifiers.

| Score | Mechanical effect |
|---|---|
| 0 | No effect. |
| 1 | Tracked, without a generic numerical penalty. |
| 2 | −1 Perception/Investigation checks specifically distinguishing similar identities, copies, duplicates or conflicting sensory impressions. Declare this scope before rolling. |
| 3 | −1 INT and WIS ability checks. |
| 4 | −1 INT, WIS and CHA ability checks. |
| 5 | Disadvantage on INT, WIS and CHA ability checks. |
| 6 | Disadvantage on INT, WIS and CHA ability checks and saves. The character remains playable with player agency. |

Record changes only from explicit reviewed effects; cap at 0–6. These mechanics never decide a character's beliefs, loves, loyalty, factual memories, conduct or hidden revelations. A player can portray blurred memories or identity pressure without surrendering character control.

**NEW Anchor Project:** In a secure Haven or equivalent safe location, complete three full consecutive project days. Each day the patient spends two hours affirming chosen memories, relationships or personal distinctions and consumes one Supply. The player chooses the content. At the end of the third full day, make a WIS save against DC `10 + current Exposure`, including the track's actual penalties. Success reduces Exposure by one; failure does not. A new reduction requires a new full project. Ordinary rest does not reduce Exposure.

Any successful positive Exposure-gain event during the attempt interrupts it, including a gain capped at 6; prevented gains do not. Already consumed Supply remains spent. Only one Anchor Project per patient can be active. Specific reviewed removal effects may work differently. Director context and later source reconciliation remain separately packaged; private narrative information does not silently add numerical penalties or erase player agency.

# Maximum HP, stat changes and HP thresholds

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED —58 exact passages:51 class records and7 feats.** The [source register](MAXIMUM_HP_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md) preserves the original procedures; [source validation](MAXIMUM_HP_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json) verifies equality and hashes. The [first captured notebook reply](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_MAXIMUM_HP_FIRST_REVIEW_PARTIAL.md) is incomplete and must be read with the [complete tail and boundary corrections](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_MAXIMUM_HP_BOUNDARIES.md) and [exact implementation closure](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_MAXIMUM_HP_FINAL_CLOSURE.md).

These rules cover the maximum-HP and threshold components supplied here. They do not promote whole feats, create companion actions, decide character advancement, or certify every monster/item/spell maximum-HP modifier.

## Recompute capacity from separate records

Keep base maximum, bonuses, reductions and systemic multipliers separate. Base maximum excludes all modifiers represented separately in this ledger. Never feed a previously modified maximum back into the formula.

First calculate the otherwise-applicable maximum:

    preSystemicMaximum = max(1, baseMaximum + compatibleBonuses − strongestMonkTrauma)

Then apply the reviewed systemic factors against that same value:

    effectiveMaximum = max(1, floor(preSystemicMaximum × systemicFactors))

Expedition Strain4+ contributes3/4 and Exhaustion4+ contributes1/2. Multiply compatible rational factors before rounding once. Base101, Flesh Warden+20, Monk trauma−9 and both factors produce42. Suppressing that trauma produces45; do not subtract the trauma again afterward.

The numerical modifier calculation does not perform lethal-track transitions. Use the separate reviewed life-state procedure when a track actually changes. Merely recomputing maximum HP must not re-kill a living collapsed survivor at track6.

Each application retains its own ID, source, owner, target, magnitude, start/end markers, presence and suppression state, arbitration group and any acquisition/creation snapshot needed for its formula. Keep records even when another stronger application wins. Suppression does not stop clocks.

## Bonuses and source identities

| Source | Bonus and update rule |
|---|---|
| Flesh Warden | +2 per Warrior level while legally equipped; capacity only |
| Wizard Conjuration specialization | +Wizard level captured when that Wizard spell creates the summon |
| Flesh Ascendant | +2 per current Wizard level of the eligible controller supplying the feature |
| Familiar Bond | Provisional +current eligible owner's character level to familiar maximum HP |
| Tenacity | +current character level |
| Tough | +twice character level when the feat was acquired; retain this snapshot |
| Tough as Nails | +2 per character level at acquisition, then +2 for each later level |
| Dark Fortitude | +2 per current character level |

**New feat integration:** distinct feat identities granting maximum HP add together unless an explicit source says otherwise. Duplicate copies of the same feat do not add. Their original acquisition/prerequisite, retraining and other-effect rules still need their separate review.

**New Wizard-specific stacking exception:** Conjuration and Flesh Ascendant add when the same undead summon qualifies for both, overriding the frozen strongest same-stat class-technique bonus default for this pair only. Flesh Ascendant's engine[24] and named card describe one modifier identity; do not count both.

When later companion lifecycle code constructs records, the engine/card aliases must share one actual effect identity, including suppression and removal. Numerical non-stacking alone must not leave a second textual alias operative after that effect is suppressed.

Conjuration's amount and caster provenance stay tied to creation. A later caster level or controller change does not recompute that snapshot. Flesh Ascendant instead follows the current eligible controller; changing control ends the old controller's eligibility and can create the new controller's eligible bonus, without healing.

**New Familiar Bond interpretation:** its ambiguous “gains hit points” wording supplies maximum capacity. Initial creation under that bonus can include it in starting HP; later level increases add capacity only. Familiar ownership/replacement and attack/command rules remain in the future companion package.

When a creature is initially created, construct its starting state from its final creation maximum unless its source expressly enters it damaged. Base20 plus Conjuration10 plus Flesh Ascendant20 gives50/50 at creation. Acquiring either bonus later does not fill missing HP. No bonus changes creature or command caps.

## Monk trauma uses one global strongest reduction

**Explicit correction of the earlier per-owner proposal:** Monk engine[9]'s categorical non-stacking clause controls. Use the largest currently operative Monk maximum-HP reduction on the target across all owners.

Ribcrusher applies S+M, Bone-Breaking Strike2S+M, and Deathless Silence4S+M. Preserve each successful application separately, including repeated applications of the same card. Do not combine the strongest magnitude with another record's longer duration. If−9 is suppressed, an operative−5 can become effective; when−5 expires, it stops contributing even while−9 remains suppressed.

Default Monk trauma ends when the target completes a short or long rest. This is effect removal, independent of how many numerical rest rewards the target already earned. Interrupted rest ends none. A genuinely explicit earlier/different endpoint controls its own record; the existence of an endpoint parameter does not grant permission to invent one.

Deathless Silence has three independent components: the Monk's protection from Reactions/opportunity attacks through source-next-regular-start; target defensive-passive suppression through that target's next-turn end; and maximum-HP trauma through the target's completed rest. Preserve the already reviewed control clocks.

## Capacity changes are not HP damage or healing

After any maximum change, clamp current normal HP down only if it exceeds the new maximum. Adding/restoring maximum HP gives no current HP. This clamp is not damage, sacrifice or healing; it creates no Wound save, death-save failure, resource trigger, redirection or first-fall event. Decay does not prevent capacity restoration.

Temporary HP is independent and remains unchanged. Maximum reduced to10 does not remove an existing25 temporary HP.

Dead, Stable and dying0 creatures retain their life state, counters and Stable deadline. A minimum maximum of1 never revives a corpse. Critical's healing ceiling recomputes afterward as max(1,effectiveMaximum−1); it is not another maximum-HP reduction.

## Exact thresholds and recorded events

Use effective maximum and integer comparison, without rounding a percentage threshold first:

| Wording | Comparison |
|---|---|
| At/below one-quarter | 4×HP ≤ maximum |
| Below one-quarter | 4×HP < maximum |
| At/below half | 2×HP ≤ maximum |
| Below half | 2×HP < maximum |
| Above half | 2×HP > maximum |

Continuous predicates update whenever HP or maximum changes: Wyrmhide, Brutality Sense, Pain Empowerment, Dark Fortitude's poison resistance, Life Drinker's conditional damage, and “below maximum” regeneration eligibility. Pain Empowerment uses full10% missing-HP bands, capped at+5, at its printed pre-roll moment.

**New first-fall interpretation:** Anointed Guardian, Burning Blood IV, Death's Threshold and Adrenal Floodgate require a genuine downward crossing. At/below-quarter triggers require HP moving from above quarter to at/below quarter. Burning Blood IV requires moving from at/above half to strictly below half. Actual damage or direct HP loss can establish a crossing unless a source specifically restricts it to damage. Capacity changes and clamps cannot.

If a rest refreshes a first-fall use while its subject is already below the threshold, neither the refresh nor another1HP loss fires it. The subject must return to the non-trigger side and cross again. Source frequency/history remains a separate eligibility gate; a crossing alone grants no new use.

Death's Threshold's exit requires actual HP restoration leaving the creature above half. A maximum reduction that makes unchanged HP above half does not end it. A later actual heal can satisfy that exit even if the creature was already above half before that heal.

**New continuous duration interpretation:** Mythic Carapace and Butcherform Chassis end when active and strictly below quarter. A maximum increase can therefore end them without damage. Exact quarter remains legal. Other duration endpoints still apply.

Record pre/post normal HP and the event-effective maximum for historical checks. Rewind Wound uses the maximum stored with its referenced damage event, never a later maximum. Freeze same-event HP crossings before a later stat clamp.

Rewind Wound requires genuine damage causing actual normal-HP decrease and leaving the target below half; it does not require a first crossing. HP40→30 at maximum100 qualifies even though both values are below half. An event entirely absorbed by temporary HP does not qualify.

Selection/rider timing follows each card: Mass Healing Light when its target is chosen; Merciful Sacrament at initial activation; Flesh to Ash before rolling damage; Death Touch at strike start; Blessing of the Meek/ Verdant Pulse before healing; Final Verdict at legal targeting; Fearbrand/Malicious Execution before their damage/rider; Echo Strike after its copied damage. Brutality Progress's already reviewed snapshot rules remain unchanged.

## Percentage recovery and damage

Use effective maximum when the amount resolves unless the source explicitly references an earlier snapshot. Floor the percentage amount, with minimum1 only where printed or already supplied by the reviewed viable-resurrection bridge.

Wound Eater III can heal0 at maximum3. Spiral III and False Life V explicitly retain minimum1 for quarter recovery. Unyielding Light uses one third with minimum1. Divine Rebirth uses the reviewed viable-return max(1,floor(maximum/2)). Wound Eater V's quarter target-HP loss and half self-heal cap retain their direct-loss classification. Ledger Unbound caps its raw damage at a quarter of target maximum before its save-halving.

Repair Pulse and Snap Rebuild use half device maximum under their own functional/destroyed target rules. A tiny-maximum reconstruction's viability belongs to the device lifecycle and is not silently converted into a general minimum1 here.

## Attack damage before Monk trauma

**New integration for the supplied Monk trauma cards:** choose/pay an after-hit option at its legal hit window. Resolve the ordinary attack's damage, Wounds, Instant Death and any survival replacement against the pre-trauma maximum; freeze its metrics. If the target remains an eligible living creature, resolve the trauma CON save using its then-current save modifier, including applicable Wound consequences. On failure, create the trauma record and recompute capacity.

If the attack leaves the target Dead, no combat-trauma record is needed and the paid cost is not refunded. A legal same-resolution death replacement preserving life can leave the target eligible.

Example: maximum30, HP30; damage4 leaves26 and records4 actual damage. A later−15 maximum reduction gives maximum15 and clamps current HP26→15. The11-point clamp causes no second damage/Wound/threshold event and cannot rewrite the attack's Instant Death threshold or concentration packet.

## Validation and remaining scope

The current reference passes60 targeted checks and909 systemic parity states. It accepts already legal source records and event snapshots; it does not decide source acquisition, perform companion creation, pay Ki, schedule turns or consume first-fall uses.

Still open: unsupplied item/spell/monster/disease/curse maximum modifiers; non-Monk reductions; exceptions applying after systemic multipliers; full feat acquisition/retraining; familiar and summon/control lifecycle; unusual device reconstruction; human balance. The58-source discussion does not close these larger domains.

operational.targets: Choose a direction for a 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide line originating from the caster. Affect all creatures whose occupied space intersects it and has origin line of effect. Origin alone does not include the caster.
operational.resolution: Each affected creature makes a Dexterity save. Roll one shared 3d8 fire: failure takes full damage; success takes half, rounded down, followed by individual defenses.
operational.effect: The line affects all actual creatures in its initial geometry, including allies, and ends immediately. Initial area recipients are a snapshot at resolution, with no selective omission or later entry damage. Apply the stated geometry and line of effect from the origin/center before damage removes cover; allies and caster are included only when the card actually includes their occupied space. Roll the stated raw area damage once, then apply each recipient’s save and defenses independently. Halved damage rounds down before individual defenses. Distinct recipients retain separate damage packets and callbacks. No attack critical applies to area save damage.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in damage, range, targets, duration, uses or magnitude.
operational.limitations: No object/structural damage, Burning, terrain fire, equipment destruction or lingering line. The possible historical name grants no extra spell identity, class access or external rules. Actual class/source access, repertoire, level, action availability, components, costs, concentration transitions, Dissonance/Refrain and cast/counter/outcome hooks follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. These actual rank-2 placements have base 3 RP; actual source modifiers and strain surcharges still apply. V is audible, S requires the ordinary usable free hand or an actual exception, and F is the ordinary class focus. A legal cast commits payment and cast-begin consequences before its Counterspell window; later failure/countering refunds nothing and restores no displaced concentration. Spell attacks use d20 + PB + actual casting modifier against AC; natural 1 misses/natural 20 hits and doubles only actual attack damage dice. Saves use DC 8 + PB + actual casting modifier and binary-save rules. Actual defenses and source-specific hooks retain their real trigger scopes. No automatic level scaling, generic upcast, new action budget or resource generation.

currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
# Spell integration rules — provisional v0.1

Use this document with the [shared class rules](CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md), the class's own engine and the [spell packet](SPELL_PLAYTEST_STARTER.md). This is a staged development layer, not an approved-book replacement or a live companion update.

## What owns each decision

| Decision | Source used for this packet |
|---|---|
| Spell identity, every school placement and per-class rank/access | Preserved `src/data/spells.js`; do not collapse different class ranks into one global rank. |
| Common RP prices and additional spell evidence | Core Systems Known Descent V2. Its spell blocks are retained with the catalog summaries. |
| Class identity, engine, spellbook/preparation and cadence exceptions | The current class playtest packet. |
| Generic Dissonance/Refrain, action limits and core conditions | Shared class playtest rules; source Core conditions remain unchanged. |
| Missing targeting, exact endpoints, concentration ambiguities and exploit limits | Explicitly provisional decisions on each spell card. |

The approved Core V2 source has 936 spell blocks. The companion catalog has 848 unique IDs with 936 school placements, but leaves four metadata fields unspecified. These are different views of the source, not evidence that all casting details were absent. Core's generic “Automatic or opposed as described” does not supply a concrete save or targeting rule.

Eleven possible renamed entries remain comparative evidence in the register. Harmonic Bulwark's catalog summary says 5 temporary HP per RP while the possible historical Mana Shield entry says 2; its [individual transformation and buffer review](TRANSFORMATION_SPELL_PLAYTEST.md) now supplies the operational decision. Both source variants remain preserved. Other unresolved aliases stay pending their own review; matching names never silently merge effects.

Resonance Kindle now has [exact manuscript approval](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CONJURATION_CANTRIP_EXACT_REVIEW.md): Action/Self/V/S, recover 1 RP only when this spell reaches resolution. Its one character-wide use is spent at legal cast start and refreshes only on a beneficial completed long rest. The comparative Mana Kindle block remains separately preserved; its broader wording does not trigger recovery from other cantrips and its historical range grants no remote recipient. The [Conjuration cantrip status](CONJURATION_CANTRIP_REVIEW_STATUS.json) records this bounded decision and the other eleven approved cards.

## Select a spell

1. Choose the class through which you are learning/casting it. Check that class's school access and minimum **class** level on the card.
2. Use that class's spell rank and Core V2 cost. A different eligible class may receive the same spell at a different rank and level.
3. Record it in your allowed known, prepared or spellbook choices. An eligible catalog entry is not an automatic grant. Wizard and Druid keep their explicit preparation systems; fallback counts apply only where the class has no more specific rule.
4. Select only a spell marked `operational-playtest-draft` in this packet, or an operational spell expressly supplied by a class card. Other records stay visible in the unfinished queue.
5. A class card and an ordinary spell with the same name remain separate records with separate acquisition and costs. Knowing one does not grant the other. Oath spells, Matrix techniques and similar class spells use their own card.

Oracle uses RC and its Mystery/Curse system. Soldier and Warrior have no general Weave access. Dragoon first gains ordinary magic at class 3; Paladin at class 2. Sufficient RP, total character level, a class feature with the same name, or a borrowed spellbook cannot bypass a gate.

## Resolve a cast at the table

1. Verify the available Action/Bonus Action/Reaction, its exact trigger, components, targets, range and line of effect. No legal target means no activation or payment. A target in an area still needs the card's eligibility. Total cover blocks direct targeting unless expressly overridden.
2. Choose a spell from your actual repertoire. Determine its class-specific rank and RP cost: rank 0–9 costs **0/2/3/5/7/10/13/17/21/26**. Add explicitly printed extra costs; Resonance Shield adds 1 RP even when the caster receives it as a cantrip. Generic Overcast is excluded.
3. Read Dissonance **before** casting. Limit = max(4, 2 + PB + max(0, casting modifier)). At limit/limit+3/limit+6, ranked spells cost +1/+2/+3 RP. At limit+6 ordinary rank-1+ casting is blocked. Cantrips have no strain surcharge but still build Refrain. An expressly granted traumatic-casting exception pays the cost and its printed trauma; it grants neither rank nor repertoire access.
4. Commit the legal cast's RP, materials and other printed costs before any attack/save or interruption. Perform its components and establish concentration if required, ending incompatible prior concentration. An ordinary missed, saved-against or countered legal cast refunds nothing and never restores displaced concentration.
5. At this cast's beginning, apply ordinary Dissonance and Refrain once: 0 base for rank 0, 1 for ranks 1–5, 2 for ranks 6–9; consecutive same-named casts add Refrain +1/+2/+3, capped at +3. First cast or a different name adds +0. Apply the class's exact protected reduction, routing or vent and any hook whose printed trigger is beginning/casting. Weapon or idle turns do not reset the previous name/Refrain unless the class expressly says so. This chronological commitment occurs before the Counterspell window; a later Reaction cast updates its own history, and resuming the earlier cast does not update that history again.
6. Open legal cast-interruption Reactions, resolving nested counters last-in, first-out. A surviving cast then resolves its effect: spell attacks are d20 + PB + the actual casting ability modifier; save DC is 8 + PB + that modifier. Use the exact card's hit/failure/success results and ordinary damage/conditions. Outcome-dependent class hooks occur only at their printed timing and with the required actual result. No automatic cantrip scaling applies. A negated spell grants no success/hit/damage effect merely because its casting cost was paid.
7. Record concentration, exact expiration, per-rest use, summon and companion command obligations. A second spell cannot supply an ungranted Action, duplicate concentration or resource reset. A readied spell commits this casting sequence at preparation; release has no second cast, cost, cadence update or Counterspell window.

Countering requires an actual operational spell or class card, its repertoire/access and a legal remaining Reaction. The ordinary Counterspell is now reviewed; it is separate from the Mage and Wizard class cards. Dispel Minor, Dispel Resonance, Dispel Magic (Lesser) and Dispel Magic use their exact individual scopes. Rank-limited dispels inspect the original generating cast's spell rank, not RP cost or the dispeller's rank. Higher and unassigned source variants retain their own unfinished status.

## Counterspell checks and interruption

The [exact notebook review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ABJURATION_RANK2_3_EXACT_REVIEW.md) confirms this authored timing interface and corrects the earlier binary-check proposal using the existing [Core roll rules](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md). This is a tabletop procedure; the pricing helper does not implement nested reactions.

Ordinary Counterspell uses its casting class's actual spellcasting ability + PB against **DC 10 + twice the triggering spell's actual rank**. The class Wizard/Mage cards retain their printed Intelligence + PB check and their own acquisition, cost, rank and recharge. Apply the existing fixed-DC task degrees and natural shifts, then collapse Critical Success/Success to success and Failure/Critical Failure to failure. No extra critical counter effect is invented. It is neither a spell attack nor a saving throw.

| Natural d20 + modifier | DC | Existing task result | Counter result |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 20 + 0 | 22 | Failure improves to Success | Success |
| 1 + 9 | 10 | Success worsens to Failure | Failure |
| 1 + 20 | 10 | Critical Success worsens to Success | Success |

The target must be an actual pending spell with a recorded rank. The Director may use hidden source data without revealing the spell's identity/rank; attempting grants no free identification. An unassigned rank is not automatically zero. A source-defined technique is not counterable merely because it spends RP or resembles magic.

A creature normally attempts Counterspell once against a particular pending cast, across its ordinary and same-named class sources. Another Reaction alone does not supply another attempt. An exact source expressly granting an additional attempt against that same cast overrides the default. After failure, another eligible creature may react; after negation there is no further trigger. Counterspell is itself a spell and can be countered. Resolve nested counters last-in, first-out and resume surviving parents without recasting, paying again, or replaying their earlier Refrain/Dissonance. Negation refunds no costs and restores no prior concentration. Countering one spell is not whole-Action/turn hard denial and does not spend that combined ledger.


## Reviewed placement-specific cards

Detect Poison has Divination rank-0 and Abjuration rank-1 modes. The casting class's preserved school/rank selects the mode; the rank-1 mode also requires F. Alignment Shield has Abjuration rank-1/30-foot and Conjuration rank-3/60-foot modes; its 60-foot header represents only the maximum range across modes. Read each full target and resolution field. These are manuscript rules; the pricing helper does not execute targeting or components.

Repulsion Field's operational entry is only the rank-1 object pulse. Its distinct rank-6 creature effect remains preserved but unavailable. Warding Bond uses its preserved rank-1 class access; the rank-2 duplicate grants no extra effect. Higher character level or extra RP never grants a blocked placement or changes modes. All source variants remain in the catalog's source evidence.

Alignment Sanctuary has Abjuration rank-3 admission saves and the actually granted Shaman Conjuration rank-6 matching-alignment mode. The unassigned rank-6 Abjuration benefits remain unavailable. Identity counts do not close every preserved placement; consult the [variant register](SPELL_VARIANT_REVIEW_STATUS.json).

Ordinary Warding Bond follows the reviewed damage-sharing stage/root rules and its exact card. It does not use or enlarge the Paladin class redirection round ledger or grant named Paladin healing/resource riders. Its authored promotion does not establish an implementation of its effect in the damage-sharing reference helper.

## Reviewed finite conjurations

The [rank-1 Conjuration review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CONJURATION_RANK1_EXACT_REVIEW.md) selects **2 RP** for Summon Mod Rod under the manifest's Core V2 spellcasting precedence; the conflicting V6/catalog 1-RP wording remains preserved. Its charge and separate character-wide caster supply/recipient receipt uses commit at activation start, including prevented or zero recovery, and refresh only on each character's beneficial completed long rest. Replacing rods never resets those records.

Read the [exact cards](SPELL_PLAYTEST_STARTER.md) for each created object's weight, native HP, duration, custody, load and ending. Summon Minor Weapon is wielded through ordinary weapon actions; it grants no attack on casting. Conjure Rope and Resonance Bridge require real support and apply ordinary Falling on failure. Alignment Essence preserves its empty result-vial for one minute after full consumption. Faction Messenger conserves supplied mundane paper and cannot resolve an ambiguous recipient description magically. Heat Metal keeps its physical-item round record and six-second next-pulse deadline through recasting, handoff and initiative changes. These are authored procedures; [review status](CONJURATION_RANK1_REVIEW_STATUS.json) does not certify runtime or balance.

## Components, summons and ongoing effects

**V** requires audible speech; **S** requires a free hand or a class feature expressly permitting the gesture; **F** is the class's ordinary casting focus. Core's M/F shorthand is interpreted here as the existing focus alternative. No unspecified costly or consumed material is added. These hand/focus conventions are provisional and may require equipment integration. A spell with V is blocked by an effect explicitly preventing verbal casting.

Summon stat blocks use their printed AC/HP/attack die. Where absent, saves use the owner's PB, other ability checks use +0, walking Speed is 30 feet, and there are no unstated creature immunities or extraordinary senses. Unless a card explicitly gives another bounded range, a commanded companion must be within 60 feet and able to perceive its owner. All one owner's companions share one Bonus Action command and **one damaging action total per round**. Without a command they move and Dodge. A replacement requires the full casting cost. No summon grants loot, a reusable corpse or resource-generating death trigger.

The [rank-2 Conjuration review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CONJURATION_RANK2_EXACT_REVIEW.md) approves this specific companion overlay: **when an exact companion source prints multiple attacks as one damaging action, those attacks are components of one commanded offensive action and consume the owner's single offensive-companion allowance unless that source expressly grants otherwise.** Summon Air Pet explicitly makes its two source attacks within that one action; no second command/action or remaining offense for another companion is created. Its fixed AC15/HP20/two 1d6 attacks do not inherit generic companion scaling.

Planar Ally (Minor) uses a finite NEW summon-only profile for the source's intended CR-1 role. The bounded public bestiary scan did not establish an eligible published exact-CR1 extraplanar creature; this card does not certify its CR or rewrite a bestiary entry. Summon Weaponry Satchel has finite conjured contents tied to one duration, with a narrow exception only for an already resolving immediate use. Alignment Weapon's suppression default applies only to that printed card.

Resonance Well rolls one 1d4 total reserve. Its separately named creation and receipt uses commit before prevention and reset only through each character's beneficial long rest. These limits neither share nor reset Kindle or Mod Rod records. Read the exact cards and [rank-2 status](CONJURATION_RANK2_REVIEW_STATUS.json); pricing/schema checks do not execute these effects or certify balance.

The [rank-3 Conjuration review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CONJURATION_RANK3_EXACT_REVIEW.md) adds seven bounded cards. Earth Pet's knockdown is Prone, not positional movement; generic push/pull immunity does not automatically prevent it. Burst of Flamewind affects every creature the caster ordinarily classifies as an enemy at a known location in its cone, with automatic source damage and a save controlling only its push.

Elemental Displacement selects a nearby willing recipient and a perceived destination; its teleport path is not constrained by intervening terrain. Spectral Steed actually crosses planes to a known site, once per steed attempt. Its 350-pound **and** 12-Load limits count the rider's body and all gear, including melded equipment. The reviewed correction from the conference's proposed6Load avoids excluding all gear from a Medium rider; ordinary Burdened applies at6Load. Read the exact mount/command/arrival procedure; it does not close general mounted combat.

Resonance Conduit transfers already-existing RP between two separate pools, with committed deductions, gated credit, and no resource creation or daily-ledger reset. Renewed consent cannot revive an ended application, but a new legal paid cast may create a new one. Faction Portal provides actual one-way travel to a known HQ on the same or another plane. Its positive-standing predicate uses the current canonical reputation record without migrating its scale. Travel may bypass a geographic route; elapsed clocks, cargo custody, contamination, claims, arrival law and settlement remain actual procedures. These cards do not declare automatic Extraction success or invent a blanket prohibition on planar escape. [Review status](CONJURATION_RANK3_REVIEW_STATUS.json) preserves the manuscript/runtime/balance distinction.

 Noncombat helpers cannot attack or operate combat items.

A cantrip that stabilizes restores no HP and removes no Wound. Mending cannot replace finite machine repair or refresh ammunition, charges, duration or class resources. Created tools, servants and water obey the explicit card limits; a spell does not silently pay wages, produce saleable materials or erase abstract expedition Supply.

All hard whole-Action/turn denial uses one combined **source-character/target/encounter** record across that character's spells, class features and companions. Once used, later hard-denial riders from that source fail; damage and soft riders resolve as printed. Boss immunities remain effective. Same-stat flat bonuses use the strongest; same-name dice bonuses do not stack. Apply one allowed bonus-die spell per roll in this packet unless a reviewed feature explicitly permits more. Temporary HP never add together. Copies never generate copies, class procs or resource loops.

## Falling bridge — new provisional procedure

This is a newly authored table procedure agreed with the GPT notebook, **not recovered V6/Core V2 canon**. Focused searches of the current rulebook extract, Core V2 and mechanics/manual text found spell summaries but no operational falling clock or impact formula. Before promotion to canon, inspect the approved V6 environment/travel/hazard sections and archived environment tables. Preserve any older rule found and compare it explicitly.

When a creature loses support with no movement mode or effect keeping it aloft, it enters **Falling** immediately. Falling means unsupported; it grants no hovering, airborne walking or lateral movement. Track total distance descended during this fall and cumulative distance during its current uncontrolled portion, both initially zero.

**Timing:** If a fall begins during a regular initiative turn, set a fixed Fall Marker at the **end of that initiative slot in the following round**. Resolve the first Falling Step there, then one at the same marker each round. Reactions and extra turns use the enclosing regular initiative slot; an event between slots uses the most recently completed slot. Extra turns, extra Actions and initiative changes neither move nor multiply the marker. This gives every participant one normal turn opportunity before the first descent; inability to act still matters and no free rescue action is granted. A caster still needs legal targets within range when spending their Action.

Outside initiative, when timing matters, establish an order before descent and use a virtual slot immediately before its first regular slot as the initiating slot. The first step occurs when that virtual slot next recurs, after everyone has had one normal turn opportunity. When no rescue or other timing decision is possible, the Director can resolve the same descent and impact calculation directly. This is an explicit timing abstraction, not a model of physical acceleration.

If a fall begins after initiative has been established but before any regular initiative slot has yet completed, treat the virtual pre-round slot as the most recently completed slot for Fall Marker purposes.

**Ordinary descent:** At each step descend up to **300 feet**, stopping on a supporting surface. Add the distance to both trackers. On landing while uncontrolled, take **min(10, floor(uncontrolled distance / 20))d6 bludgeoning damage**. The uncontrolled distance includes earlier steps; never use only the final step's remainder.

**Feather Fall:** The spell retains its **Action** casting time and reduces descent to at most **60 feet per step**. When it takes effect, set uncontrolled distance to zero: the magic dissipates prior uncontrolled momentum in this abstraction. Keep total fall distance. If landing while it remains active, damage is **min(3, floor(total fall distance / 20))d6 bludgeoning**. This explicitly limits impact exposure without guaranteeing a harmless landing. When the spell ends aloft, reset uncontrolled distance to zero, then accumulate ordinary descent from that point at the existing marker; expiry grants no immediate extra step. Its one-minute maximum ends immediately before the caster's regular turn ten rounds after casting. If expiry and a step coincide, resolve expiry first. Earlier landing or cessation of Falling ends the spell on that target as printed.

Apply damage defenses only when their actual wording covers that damage. After damage, Falling ends; a creature suffering any positive falling damage lands **Prone** unless an explicit feature prevents it. Less than 20 relevant feet produces zero damage. Forced movement that removes support starts a fall but adds no separate fall damage. Regaining genuine support, secure support from a hold, or flight ends Falling without resolving an uncompleted impact; teleporting safely onto support likewise ends it. A later loss of support begins a new fall with new trackers and marker. Completed impact and damage cannot be undone by later casting.

| Scenario | Steps to land | Impact |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ordinary 10 feet | 1 | 0 |
| Ordinary 20 feet | 1 | 1d6 |
| Ordinary 300 feet | 1 | 10d6 |
| Ordinary 310 feet | 2 | 10d6 |
| Ordinary 610 feet | 3 | 10d6 |
| Feather Fall active through a 310-foot fall | 6 | 3d6 |
| 120 feet slowed, spell ends aloft, then 190 feet uncontrolled | 3 | 9d6 |

The 300-foot ordinary step, impact formulas, momentum reset, marker and duration conventions are provisional inventions. The source supplies Feather Fall's Action, five targets and 60-foot slowed descent. Wider hazards, equipment catches, flight loss and environmental damage still need the combat/campaign pass.

## Recovery bridge and unresolved integration

The class suite's **Retune** formula is the active RP rule for this combined test: recover max(0, floor(maxRP/4 + 0.5) + actual casting modifier), capped at maximum, and clear Dissonance after a completed one-hour short rest. Retain the expedition rule of at most **two beneficial short rests between long rests**, and one beneficial eight-hour long rest per **24 hours**. A long rest restores RP and clears Dissonance; expedition time, supply, pressure, Wounds and rest legality still apply. Count time once, not once in each tracker. Oracle and other non-RP engines use their class-specific recovery, not this formula.

This bridge explicitly chooses the class Retune formula over the gameplay draft's quarter-pool-only RP paragraph. Both originals remain preserved. A completed long rest also resets the remembered spell name and Refrain counter. A short rest clears Dissonance through Retune but does not reset Refrain unless a class feature expressly says so. This reset convention is an explicit provisional decision agreed in the notebook review. Broader recovery decisions for all class resources still require the character/campaign integration pass.

## Developer verification

`tools/spell_playtest_rules.py` checks operational status, class access, level gates, known/prepared membership and the **common pricing step**. Its Dissonance result is deliberately labelled *before class interface*. The caller must apply the actual protected class cadence or vent and verify actions, components, target legality, concentration and effect resolution. This helper is not an automatic implementation of every spell or class.

Run `python tools/build_spell_playtests.py`, then `python tools/validate_spell_playtests.py`. Source accounting, metadata coverage, access boundaries and cost/reference scenarios are independently reported. A passing result does not certify the remaining catalog, all cross-class combinations, human balance or live-app readiness.

`tools/fall_playtest_rules.py` separately exercises the new falling marker and distance/impact calculation. Callers still own actual spell availability/expiry, support, actions, damage rolls, defenses and Prone. Its regression cases specifically prevent premature or duplicate steps, harmless remainder exploits and retroactive changes to resolved landings.


## Reviewed Divination cantrip information boundaries

The [eleven-card review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_DIVINATION_CANTRIP_EXACT_REVIEW.md) and [final source clarification](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_DIVINATION_CANTRIP_FINAL_CLARIFICATION.md) make each spell's information output explicit. Actual hidden facts may be revealed when a spell authorizes them; undefined records must not be invented. Sense Alignment distinguishes recorded axes, Indeterminate and genuinely unaligned objects. Detect Faction requires an actual affiliation/nonaffiliation record; absence of a field is not a negative finding. Resonance Sight reads current RP only, using ordinary visibility and actual pools; unreadability is not proof of no pool.

Protection from Scrying prevents new information about its subject within its actual generating-school scope, including new Far Echo retrieval. It does not erase events, ordinary recordings or known facts, nor grant blanket immunity to Foresight Flicker's roll modifier or Glimpse Future's initiative benefit. Soul Mark's record can remain while its directional information is blocked. The final clarification retains the source's creature eligibility: active creature-classified Undead/Construct targets are not excluded merely by type. Death/destruction/ended summoned existence ends the mark; ordinary shapechange or travel alone does not.

Omen Whisper limits materially equivalent inquiries across casters, while genuinely different material questions can receive another clue. Far Echo uses speech produced in its fixed capture sphere and actually audible at the center in the six seconds before casting. Read Surface Thoughts yields one actual current conscious thought after its save, not memories or forced truth. Detect Weather supplies an accurate current-trajectory forecast; a later actual new cause may alter it, with that cause recorded in the game. These are authored procedures, not a complete information/weather engine or balance certification. See [review status](DIVINATION_CANTRIP_REVIEW_STATUS.json).


## Mark Omen and Fate Coin: reviewed spell-specific rerolls

Mark Omen and Fate Coin share one guard: an original roll event and its entire replacement lineage may receive at most one reroll from either of these two spells, across all casters, coins, marks and recasts. Reserve this allowance at the first legal activation's commitment, not after the replacement die resolves. For a multi-die roll, the whole set/pool is one original roll event; the resulting attack's separate later damage roll is a different event. A shared area-damage roll remains one event even when applied to several creatures. Other exact class reroll features keep their own permissions and timing, but do not erase this guard or create a fresh lineage for these two spells. If competing declarations are simultaneous, use current initiative order; outside initiative use a fixed neutral table order chosen before the roll. Only the first legal commitment spends a mark/coin; a later declaration barred by this guard spends nothing. No new Action, roll event, cast, payment or duplicated outcome hook is created by replacing dice.

currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Which rule applies

The domain authority is [Core Systems Known Descent V2](../../../../books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx). The approved [Player Rulebook V6](../../../../books/player/Decennium_Descent_Player_Rulebook_v6.docx) supplies compatible rules that Core does not replace. This overlay states the selected interpretation or newly authored rule wherever those sources leave a gap. An explicit exception on an operative, reviewed class/spell/item card applies only within its printed scope; a historical alternate or a same-named feature is not an extra grant. This candidate does not promote an entire historical branch.

| Question | Active rule and provenance | Inactive alternate |
|---|---|---|
